      while IFS=: read -r l_file l_mode l_user l_group; do
         file_access_chk
      done <<< "$(stat -Lc '"'"'%n:%#a:%U:%G'"'"' "$l_gfile")"
   done < <(find /boot -type f \( -name '"'"'grub*'"'"' -o -name '"'"'user.cfg'"'"' \) - print0)
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}" ""
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

audit.command: chk() { p=$1; allowed=" $2 "; case $p in net.ipv6.*) [ -d /proc/sys/net/ipv6 ] || return 0;; esac; v=$(sysctl -n "$p" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$p: not available"; return 1; }; case "$allowed" in *" $v "*) ;; *) echo "$p is $v (running)"; return 1;; esac; sd=$(readlink -e /lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl || readlink -e /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl); f=$("$sd" --cat-config 2>/dev/null | grep -Po "^\h*${p//./\.}\h*=\h*\K\H+" | tail -n1); [ -n "$f" ] || { echo "$p is not set in any sysctl configuration file"; return 1; }; case "$allowed" in *" $f "*) ;; *) echo "$p is $f in configuration"; return 1;; esac; }; if chk kernel.randomize_va_space 2; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure /etc/motd is configured
description: The contents of the /etc/motd file are displayed to users after login and function as a message of the day for authenticated users. Unix-based systems have typically displayed information about the OS release and patch level upon logging in to the system. This information can be useful to developers who are developing software for a particular OS platform. If mingetty(8) supports the following options, they display operating system information: \m - machine architecture \r - operating system release \s - operating system name \v - operating system version

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_output="" l_output2=""
   a_files=()
   for l_file in /etc/motd{,.d/*}; do
      if grep -Psqi -- "(\\\v|\\\r|\\\m|\\\s|\b$(grep ^ID= /etc/os-release | cut -d= -f2 | sed -e '"'"'s/"//g'"'"')\b)" "$l_file"; then
         l_output2="$l_output2\n - File: \"$l_file\" includes system information"
      else
         a_files+=("$l_file")
      fi
   done
   if [ "${#a_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo -e "\n-  ** Please review the following files and verify their contents follow local site policy **\n"
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "${a_files[@]}"
   elif [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then
      echo -e "- ** No MOTD files with any size were found. Please verify this conforms to local site policy ** -"
   fi
   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then
      l_output=" - No MOTD files include system information"
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** PASS **\n$l_output\n"
   else
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n - Reason(s) for audit failure:\n$l_output2\n"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; return 0; }
tma_ini_set() { # file section key value
  local f=$1 s=$2 k=$3 v=$4
  [ -e "$f" ] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; : > "$f"; }
  tma_bak "$f"
  awk -v s="$s" -v k="$k" -v v="$v" '
    function flush() { if (insec && !done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } }
    /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { flush(); insec = ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*\\[" s "\\][[:space:]]*$"); print; next }
    insec && $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*" k "[[:space:]]*=" { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } ; next }
    { print }
    END { flush(); if (!done) { print "[" s "]"; print k "=" v } }' "$f" > "$f.tma" && cat "$f.tma" > "$f"; rm -f "$f.tma"
}
tma_grub_regen() {
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ -f /boot/grub2/grub.cfg ]; then grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg
    else for c in /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c"; done; fi
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -f /boot/grub/grub.cfg ] && grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
  fi; return 0
}
tma_cmdline_rm() { # names of kernel args (name or name=value) to drop from the grub defaults
  local a f c k n
  for a in "$@"; do
    for f in /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.d/*.cfg; do
      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" "$f" || continue
      tma_bak "$f"
      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"
    done
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args="$a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  if command -v grub2-editenv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    k=$(grub2-editenv - list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^kernelopts=//p')
    if [ -n "$k" ]; then n=$k; for a in "$@"; do n=$(printf '%s' "$n" | sed -E "s/(^| )${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/ /g"); done
      [ "$n" != "$k" ] && grub2-editenv - set "kernelopts=$n"; fi
  fi
  for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/grub/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do
    [ -f "$c" ] || continue
    for a in "$@"; do sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*(linux|kernelopts)/ s/(^|[ =])${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/\1\3/g" "$c"; done
  done
  return 0
}
tma_cmdline_set() { # name=value pairs forced into GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
  local f=/etc/default/grub kv; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $f"; return 0; }
  for kv in "$@"; do
    tma_cmdline_rm "${kv%%=*}" "${kv%%=*}=[^ \"']*" 2>/dev/null
    tma_bak "$f"
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$f"; then
      sed -i -E "s/^([[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=[\"'])(.*)([\"'])\$/\1\2 ${kv}\3/; s/=([\"']) /=\1/" "$f"
    else printf 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="%s"\n' "$kv" >> "$f"; fi
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --args="$kv" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  return 0
}
prof=local
mkdir -p /etc/dconf/profile /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks
pf() { [ -f "$1" ] || : > "$1"; while IFS= read -r l; do grep -qxF "$l" "$1" || printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$1"; done; }
printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user
system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/$prof
printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user' 'system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/user
cat > /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/00-media-automount <<'TMAEOF'
[org/gnome/desktop/media-handling]
automount=false
automount-open=false
TMAEOF
printf '%s\n' /org/gnome/desktop/media-handling/automount /org/gnome/desktop/media-handling/automount-open > /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks/00-media-automount
command -v dconf >/dev/null 2>&1 && dconf update
true

title: Ensure mail transfer agents are configured for local-only mode
description: Mail Transfer Agents (MTA), such as sendmail and Postfix, are used to listen for incoming mail and transfer the messages to the appropriate user or mail server. If the system is not intended to be a mail server, it is recommended that the MTA be configured to only process local mail.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=(); a_port_list=("25" "465" "587")
   for l_port_number in "${a_port_list[@]}"; do
      if ss -plntu | grep -P -- '"'"':'"'"'"$l_port_number"'"'"'\b'"'"' | grep -Pvq -- '"'"'\h+(127\.0\.0\.1|\[?::1\]?):'"'"'"$l_port_number"'"'"'\b'"'"'; then
         a_output2+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is listening on a non- loopback network interface")
      else
         a_output+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is not listening on a non- loopback network interface")
      fi
   done
   if command -v postconf &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(postconf -n inet_interfaces)"
   elif command -v exim &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(exim -bP local_interfaces)"
   elif command -v sendmail &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(grep -i "O DaemonPortOptions=" /etc/mail/sendmail.cf | grep -oP '"'"'(?<=Addr=)[^,+]+'"'"' | grep -v '"'"'^127\.0\.0\.1$'"'"')"
   fi
   if [ -n "$l_interfaces" ]; then
      if grep -Pqi '"'"'\ball\b'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to all network interfaces")
      elif ! grep -Pqi '"'"'(inet_interfaces\h*=\h*)?(0\.0\.0\.0|::1|loopback- only|localhost)'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to a network interface" " \"$l_interfaces\"")
      else
         a_output+=(" - MTA is not bound to a non loopback network interface" "   \"$l_interfaces\"")
      fi
   else
      a_output+=(" - MTA not detected or in use")
   fi
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"
      exit "${XCCDF_RESULT_PASS:-101}"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"
      exit "${XCCDF_RESULT_FAIL:-102}"

title: Ensure root user umask is configured
description: The user file-creation mode mask (umask) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (rwxrwxrwx), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (rw-rw- rw-). The umask modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The umask is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the umask are cleared in the resulting file mode. umask can be set with either Octal or Symbolic values: • Octal (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four

title: Ensure world writable files and directories are secured
description: World writable files are the least secure. Data in world-writable files can be modified and compromised by any user on the system. World writable files may also indicate an incorrectly written script or program that could potentially be the cause of a larger compromise to the system's integrity. See the chmod(2) man page for more information. Setting the sticky bit on world writable directories prevents users from deleting or renaming files in that directory that are not owned by them.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=() a_output2=() a_file=() a_dir=()

   a_path=(-path "*/containers/storage/*" -o -path "*/containerd/*" -o -path "*/kubelet/*" -o -path "/sys/*" -o -path "/snap/*" -o -path "/boot/efi/*")
   while IFS= read -r l_mount; do
      while IFS= read -r -d $'"'"'\0'"'"' l_file; do
         if [ -e "$l_file" ]; then
            [ -f "$l_file" ] && a_file+=("$l_file")
            if [ -d "$l_file" ]; then
               l_mode="$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a'"'"' "$l_file")"
               [ ! $(( $l_mode & $l_smask )) -gt 0 ] && a_dir+=("$l_file")
            fi
         fi

   done < <(findmnt -Dkerno fstype,target | awk '"'"'($1 !~ /^\s*(nfs|proc|cifs|smb|vfat|iso9660|efivarfs|selinuxfs|ncpfs)/ && $2 !~ /^(\/run|\/tmp|\/var\/tmp)(\/|$)/){print $2}'"'"')
   if [ "${#a_file[@]}" -le 0 ]; then

   else
      a_output2+=("" " - There are \"${#a_file[@]}\" World writable files on the system." \
      "   - The following is a list of World writable files:" \
      "${a_file[@]:0:$l_limit}" "   - end of list")

   if [ "${#a_dir[@]}" -le 0 ]; then

   else

title: Ensure SELinux is not disabled in bootloader configuration
description: Configure SELINUX to be enabled at boot time and verify that it has not been overwritten by the grub boot parameters.

audit.command: alt0() { o=$(bash -c 'grubby --info=ALL | grep -Po '"'"'(selinux|enforcing)=0\b'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Prs -- '"'"'^\h*([^#\n\r]+\h+)?kernelopts=([^#\n\r]+\h+)?(selinux|enforcing)=0\b'"'"' /boot/grub2 /boot/efi' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step2: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure the MCS Translation Service (mcstrans) is not installed
description: The mcstransd daemon provides category label information to client processes requesting information. The label translations are defined in /etc/selinux/targeted/setrans.conf

audit.command: alt0() { command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: rpm not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'rpm -q mcstrans' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'package mcstrans is not installed' || { echo step1: missing 'package mcstrans is not installed'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to uninstall mcstrans: # dnf remove mcstrans

title: Ensure SETroubleshoot is not installed
description: The SETroubleshoot service notifies desktop users of SELinux denials through a user- friendly interface. The service provides important information around configuration errors, unauthorized intrusions, and other potential errors.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: rpm not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'rpm -q setroubleshoot' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'package setroubleshoot is not installed' || { echo step1: missing 'package setroubleshoot is not installed'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to uninstall setroubleshoot: # dnf remove setroubleshoot

title: Ensure systemd ability to spawn an interactive boot process is disabled
description: The systemd.confirm_spawn kernel argument causes systemd to prompt interactively at the console before spawning each unit during boot. Removing this argument prevents an interactive boot process.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grubby not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grubby --info=ALL | grep -E '"'"'^\s*args='"'"' | grep '"'"'systemd.confirm_spawn'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to remove the systemd.confirm_spawn argument from all boot entries: # grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args=systemd.confirm_spawn Then edit /etc/default/grub and remove systemd.confirm_spawn from the GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX (and GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT) line so it is not reintroduced on the next kernel or bootloader update. If the system uses /etc/kernel/cmdline, remove it there as well.

set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";

tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }

tma_ini_set() { # file section key value
  local f=$1 s=$2 k=$3 v=$4

}

  for a in "$@"; do

      tma_bak "$f"
      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"

title: Ensure access to /etc/crontab is configured
description: The /etc/crontab file is used by cron to control its own jobs. The commands in this item make sure that root is the user and group owner of the file and that only the owner can access the file.

audit.command: alt0() { s=$(stat -Lc '%a %u %g' /etc/crontab 2>&1) || { echo "step1: $s"; return 1; }; set -- $s; m=$((8#$1)); [ $((m & ~0600)) -eq 0 ] && [ "$2" = 0 ] && [ "$3" = 0 ] || { echo "step1: /etc/crontab is mode $1 uid $2 gid $3, want 600 or stricter, uid 0, gid 0"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: - IF - cron is installed on the system: Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on /etc/crontab: # chown root:root /etc/crontab # chmod og-rwx /etc/crontab

description: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology standard that is used for exchanging data between devices over short distances. It employs UHF radio waves in the ISM bands, from 2.402 GHz to 2.48 GHz. It is mainly used as an alternative to wire connections.

title: Ensure dccp kernel module is not available
description: The Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP) is a transport layer protocol that supports streaming media and telephony. DCCP provides a way to gain access to congestion control, without having to do it at the application layer, but does not provide in-sequence delivery.

audit.command: m=dccp; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/dccp*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

title: Ensure all users last password change date is in the past
description: All users should have a password change date in the past.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
 while IFS= read -r l_user; do

 [ "$l_change_raw" = "never" ] && continue

title: Ensure root is the only UID 0 account
description: On a Linux system, the user ID (UID) 0 is the superuser identity: the kernel grants any account assigned UID 0 complete, unrestricted control of the host, regardless of the account's name. The root account holds UID 0 by default.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: awk not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'awk -F: '"'"'($3 == 0) { print $1 }'"'"' /etc/passwd' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'Only root should be returned.' || { echo step1: missing 'Only root should be returned.'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: 1. Run the following command to reassign any account other than root that has UID 0 to a new, unused UID (and update ownership of that account's files): # usermod -u <NEW_UID> <username> Example: # usermod -u 1234 bsmith 2. If the root account's UID is not 0, run the following command to reset it: # usermod -u 0 root

title: Ensure group root is the only GID 0 group

title: Ensure root path integrity
description: The PATH variable for the root user determines the directories the shell searches for executables when root runs a command that is not given as an absolute path. Its integrity depends on the ownership, permissions, and composition of the directories it lists.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_pmask="0022"

   grep -Pq -- ":\h*$" <<< "$l_root_path" && echo " - root'"'"'s PATH ends with a trailing colon (:)"
   grep -Pq -- '"'"'(^\h*|:)\.(:|\h*$)'"'"' <<< "$l_root_path" && echo " - root'"'"'s PATH contains the current working directory (.)"
   IFS=":" read -ra a_path_loc <<< "$l_root_path"
   for l_path in "${a_path_loc[@]}"; do
      if [ -d "$l_path" ]; then
         while IFS=: read -r l_fmode l_fown; do
            [ "$l_fown" != "root" ] && echo " - Directory \"$l_path\" is owned by \"$l_fown\" (should be owned by root)"
            [ $(( l_fmode & l_pmask )) -gt 0 ] && echo " - Directory \"$l_path\" is mode \"$l_fmode\" (should be 0755 or more restrictive)"
         done <<< "$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a:%U'"'"' "$l_path")"
      else
         echo " - \"$l_path\" is not an existing directory"
      fi
   done
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

Edit the shell initialization file that sets root's PATH (for example /root/.bash_profile, /root/.bashrc, or the relevant file under /etc/profile.d/) and remove any current-working- directory (.) entry, any empty entry (::), and any trailing colon (:). title: Ensure accounts without a valid login shell are locked
description: There are a number of accounts provided with most distributions that are used to manage applications. Additionally, an administrator may add special accounts that are not intended for interactive use.

alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{

title: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured
description: TMOUT is a shell environment variable that sets an interactive shell's idle timeout, in seconds: after TMOUT seconds with no input, the shell exits. TMOUT=<n> sets the timeout to n seconds (a value of 0 disables it); marking the variable readonly prevents a user from overriding it during the session, and exporting it applies it to the user's shell environment.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash
{
   l_max=900
   a_files=()
   while IFS= read -r l_file; do a_files+=("$l_file"); done < <(grep -Pls -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT\b'"'"' \
      /etc/*bashrc /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/*.sh /etc/profile.d/sh.local \
      /usr/etc/profile.d/*.sh /usr/etc/profile.d/sh.local 2>/dev/null)
   l_set=0
   for l_file in "${a_files[@]}"; do
      l_val="$(grep -Po -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT=\d+\b'"'"' "$l_file" | awk -F= '"'"'{v=$2} END{if (NR>0) print v}'"'"')"
      [ -z "$l_val" ] && continue
      l_set=1
      l_ro="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\- xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\breadonly\h+TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
      l_exp="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\- xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\bexport\b([^#\n\r]+\b)?TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
      [ "$l_val" -gt 0 ] && [ "$l_val" -le "$l_max" ] || echo "$l_file: TMOUT=$l_val is out of range (must be >0 and <=$l_max)"
      [ -n "$l_ro" ]  || echo "$l_file: TMOUT is not marked readonly"
      [ -n "$l_exp" ] || echo "$l_file: TMOUT is not exported"
   done
   [ "$l_set" -eq 0 ] && echo "TMOUT is not set in any shell initialization file"
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_ts=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$tma_ts"; }
tma_applied() { return 0; }

# make every umask line in the given files at least 027
tma_umask_fix() { for f in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  grep -Eqi '^[[:space:]]*umask[[:space:]]' "$f" || continue
  t=$(mktemp); ch=0
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    if [[ $line =~ ^([[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+)0*([0-7]{1,4})([[:space:]#].*)?$ ]]; then
      v=$((8#${BASH_REMATCH[2]})); n=$((v | 8#027))
      if [ "$n" != "$v" ]; then line="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}$(printf '%03o' $n)${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"; ch=1; fi
    elif [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+[ugoa]*= ]] && [[ $line =~ (g=[rwx]*w|o=[rwx]*[rwx]) ]]; then
      line="umask 027"; ch=1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$t"
  done < "$f"
  if [ $ch = 1 ]; then tma_bak "$f"; cat "$t" > "$f"; fi
  rm -f "$t"
done; }
N=900
# one authoritative file; any other TMOUT assignment is commented out (audit demands readonly+export in each file mentioning it)
for f in /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile.d/*.sh; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  [ "$f" = /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh ] && continue
  grep -Eq '^[^#]*\bTMOUT\b' "$f" || continue
  tma_bak "$f"; sed -i -E '/^[[:space:]]*#/! s/^([^#]*\bTMOUT\b.*)$/# tmaegis: \1/' "$f"
done
mkdir -p /etc/profile.d
printf '# CIS: idle shell timeout\nTMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
for f in /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile; do [ -f "$f" ] && ! grep -q '^TMOUT=' "$f" && [ "$f" = /etc/bash/bashrc ] && printf 'TMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" >> "$f"; done
true

title: Ensure journald service is active
description: systemd-journald is the systemd journaling service that collects and stores system log data. It is a static, socket-activated unit that is always present as the initial collector of log events on a systemd-based system; it is started by systemd rather than enabled to start on boot.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: systemctl not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'systemctl is-active systemd-journald.service' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- active || { echo step1: missing active; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to unmask and start systemd-journald.service: # systemctl unmask systemd-journald.service # systemctl start systemd-journald.service

title: Ensure access to rsyslog configuration files is configured
description: The main rsyslog configuration file /etc/rsyslog.conf and the drop-in configuration files ending in .conf under /etc/rsyslog.d/ control how rsyslog collects, filters, stores, and forwards system log data. These files should be owned by root, group-owned by root, and no more permissive than mode 0640, so that they can be modified only by root and are not readable by any account other than root.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: find not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'find /etc/rsyslog.conf -not -type l \( ! -user root -o ! -group root -o - perm /0137 \) 2>/dev/null' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: find not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'find /etc/rsyslog.d/ -type f -name '"'"'*.conf'"'"' \( ! -user root -o ! -group root -o -perm /0137 \) 2>/dev/null' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step2: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to set ownership to root:root and remove group write, all access for other accounts, and all execute bits from the rsyslog configuration files, resulting in mode 0640 or more restrictive: # chown root:root /etc/rsyslog.conf # chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx /etc/rsyslog.conf # find /etc/rsyslog.d/ -type f -name '*.conf' -exec chown root:root {} + # find /etc/rsyslog.d/ -type f -name '*.conf' -exec chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx {} +

title: Ensure access to the /etc/rsyslog.d directory is configured
description: The /etc/rsyslog.d/ directory holds drop-in rsyslog configuration files ending in .conf. The directory should be owned by root, group-owned by root, and not writable by any account other than root so that unauthorized users cannot add, remove, or replace rsyslog configuration fragments.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: find not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'find /etc/rsyslog.d/ -maxdepth 0 -type d \( ! -user root -o ! -group root - o -perm /0022 \) 2>/dev/null' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to set ownership to root:root and remove group and other write from the directory: # chown root:root /etc/rsyslog.d # chmod g-w,o-w /etc/rsyslog.d

title: Ensure access to the rsyslog work directory is configured
description: rsyslog's work directory, set by the global $WorkDirectory / global(workDirectory=...) directive and defaulting to /var/lib/rsyslog, stores disk-assisted queue spool files. These files can hold buffered log data written to disk when in-memory queues are exhausted or a forwarding action is retrying. The work directory should be owned by root, group- owned by root, and accessible only to root.

audit.command: alt0() { o=$(bash -c 'grep -Psi -- '"'"'^[^#]*(WorkDirectory|workDirectory)\s*[= ]'"'"' /etc/rsyslog.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf 2>/dev/null' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: find not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'find /var/lib/rsyslog -maxdepth 0 -type d \( ! -user root -o ! -group root -o -perm /0077 \) 2>/dev/null' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step2: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to set ownership to root:root and remove all group and other access from the work directory (substitute a non-default $WorkDirectory path if configured): # chown root:root /var/lib/rsyslog # chmod go-rwx /var/lib/rsyslog

title: Ensure rsyslog is not configured as a log server
description: rsyslog can be configured to receive log messages from remote hosts over the network by loading a remote-input module (imtcp, imudp, imptcp, or imrelp) and starting a listener, which makes the host act as a central log server.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{

      for l_f in $l_inc; do

title: Ensure report_url is configured
description: The report_url directive in aide.conf names the destination(s) to which AIDE writes each integrity check's report. It accepts multiple destinations and supports a syslog:<facility> target - where <facility> is a syslog facility, such as one of LOG_LOCAL0 through LOG_LOCAL7 - that sends the report to the system log rather than, or in addition to, a local file. AIDE has no built-in mail transport; syslog is its native mechanism for directing the report to the system logging service.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -P '"'"'^\h*report_url'"'"' /etc/aide.conf' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'A report_url directive sending the report to syslog should be returned, for example:' || { echo step1: missing 'A report_url directive sending the report to syslog should b'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u

tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do

tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do

  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";

tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; return 0; }
tma_ini_set() { # file section key value
  local f=$1 s=$2 k=$3 v=$4
  [ -e "$f" ] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; : > "$f"; }
  tma_bak "$f"
  awk -v s="$s" -v k="$k" -v v="$v" '
    function flush() { if (insec && !done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } }
    /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { flush(); insec = ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*\\[" s "\\][[:space:]]*$"); print; next }
    insec && $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*" k "[[:space:]]*=" { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } ; next }
    { print }
    END { flush(); if (!done) { print "[" s "]"; print k "=" v } }' "$f" > "$f.tma" && cat "$f.tma" > "$f"; rm -f "$f.tma"
}
tma_grub_regen() {
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ -f /boot/grub2/grub.cfg ]; then grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg
    else for c in /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c"; done; fi
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -f /boot/grub/grub.cfg ] && grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
  fi; return 0
}
tma_cmdline_rm() { # names of kernel args (name or name=value) to drop from the grub defaults
  local a f c k n
  for a in "$@"; do
    for f in /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.d/*.cfg; do
      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" "$f" || continue

      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"
    done
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args="$a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  if command -v grub2-editenv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    k=$(grub2-editenv - list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^kernelopts=//p')
    if [ -n "$k" ]; then n=$k; for a in "$@"; do n=$(printf '%s' "$n" | sed -E "s/(^| )${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/ /g"); done

    [ -f "$c" ] || continue
    for a in "$@"; do sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*(linux|kernelopts)/ s/(^|[ =])${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/\1\3/g" "$c"; done
  done
  return 0
}
tma_cmdline_set() { # name=value pairs forced into GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
  local f=/etc/default/grub kv; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $f"; return 0; }
  for kv in "$@"; do
    tma_cmdline_rm "${kv%%=*}" "${kv%%=*}=[^ \"']*" 2>/dev/null
    tma_bak "$f"
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$f"; then
      sed -i -E "s/^([[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=[\"'])(.*)([\"'])\$/\1\2 ${kv}\3/; s/=([\"']) /=\1/" "$f"

    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --args="$kv" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  return 0
}
for f in /etc/aide.conf /etc/aide/aide.conf; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; tma_bak "$f"

title: Ensure world writable files and directories are secured
description: World writable files are the least secure. Data in world-writable files can be modified and compromised by any user on the system. World writable files may also indicate an incorrectly written script or program that could potentially be the cause of a larger compromise to the system's integrity. See the chmod(2) man page for more information. Setting the sticky bit on world writable directories prevents users from deleting or renaming files in that directory that are not owned by them.

alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

   while IFS= read -r l_mount; do

         \( \( -type f -perm -0002 \) -o \( -type d -perm -0002 ! -perm -1000 \) \) \

}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure local interactive user home directories are configured
description: The user home directory is space defined for the particular user to set local environment variables and to store personal files. title: Ensure hfsplus kernel module is not available
description: The hfsplus filesystem type is a hierarchical filesystem designed to replace hfs that allows you to mount Mac OS filesystems.

audit.command: m=hfsplus; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/hfsplus*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Unload and disable the hfsplus kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the hfsplus kernel module: # modprobe -r hfsplus 2>/dev/null # rmmod hfsplus 2>/dev/null 2. Perform the following to disable the hfsplus kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install hfsplus /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory. Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "install hfsplus /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60- hfsplus.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist hfsplus in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory. Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "blacklist hfsplus" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-hfsplus.conf

title: Ensure /tmp is tmpfs or a separate partition
description: The /tmp directory is a world-writable directory used for temporary storage by all users and some applications. Note: If an entry for /tmp exists in /etc/fstab it will take precedence over entries in a systemd unit file. There is an exception to this when a system is diskless and connected to iSCSI, entries in /etc/fstab may not take precedence over a systemd unit file.

audit.command: if findmnt -kn /tmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo compliant; else echo /tmp' is not a separate partition'; fi

remediation.guidance: First ensure that systemd is correctly configured to ensure that /tmp will be mounted at boot time. # systemctl unmask tmp.mount For specific configuration requirements of the /tmp mount for your environment, modify /etc/fstab. Example of using tmpfs with specific mount options: tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,size=2G 0 0 Note: the size=2G is an example of setting a specific size for tmpfs. Example of using a volume or disk with specific mount options. The source location of the volume or disk will vary depending on your environment: <device> /tmp <fstype> defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec 0 0

title: Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition
description: The nodev mount option specifies that the filesystem cannot contain special devices.

audit.command: if ! findmnt -kn /tmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo compliant; elif findmnt -kn /tmp | grep -qw -- nodev; then echo compliant; else echo /tmp' is mounted without nodev'; fi

remediation.guidance: - IF - a separate partition exists for /tmp. Edit the /etc/fstab file and add nodev to the fourth field (mounting options) for the /tmp partition. Example: <device> /tmp <fstype> defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0 Run the following command to remount /tmp with the configured options: # mount -o remount /tmp

title: Ensure SELinux is not disabled in bootloader configuration
description: Configure SELINUX to be enabled at boot time and verify that it has not been overwritten by the grub boot parameters.

audit.command: alt0() { o=$(bash -c 'grubby --info=ALL | grep -Po '"'"'(selinux|enforcing)=0\b'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Prs -- '"'"'^\h*([^#\n\r]+\h+)?kernelopts=([^#\n\r]+\h+)?(selinux|enforcing)=0\b'"'"' /boot/grub2 /boot/efi' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step2: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

description: Avahi is a free zeroconf implementation, including a system for multicast DNS/DNS-SD service discovery. title: Ensure dccp kernel module is not available
description: The Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP) is a transport layer protocol that supports streaming media and telephony. DCCP provides a way to gain access to congestion control, without having to do it at the application layer, but does not provide in-sequence delivery.

audit.command: m=dccp; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/dccp*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance:
Unload and disable the dccp kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the dccp kernel module: # modprobe -r dccp 2>/dev/null # rmmod dccp 2>/dev/null 2. Perform the following to disable the dccp kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install dccp /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '
%s
' "install dccp /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-dccp.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist dccp in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '
%s
' "blacklist dccp" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-dccp.conf

title: Ensure net.ipv4.ip_forward is configured
description: The net.ipv4.ip_forward flag tells the system whether it can forward IPv4 packets or not. Note: • If this system is a router this recommendation is not applicable. • If net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding=0 and net.ipv4.conf.default.forwarding=0 are configured, this recommendation may be skipped.

audit.command: chk() { p=$1; allowed=" $2 "; case $p in net.ipv6.*) [ -d /proc/sys/net/ipv6 ] || return 0;; esac; v=$(sysctl -n "$p" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$p: not available"; return 1; }; case "$allowed" in *" $v "*) ;; *) echo "$p is $v (running)"; return 1;; esac; sd=$(readlink -e /lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl || readlink -e /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl); f=$("$sd" --cat-config 2>/dev/null | grep -Po "^\h*${p//./\.}\h*=\h*\K\H+" | tail -n1); [ -n "$f" ] || { echo "$p is not set in any sysctl configuration file"; return 1; }; case "$allowed" in *" $f "*) ;; *) echo "$p is $f in configuration"; return 1;; esac; }; if chk net.ipv4.ip_forward 0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter is configured
description: net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter controls reverse path filtering for IPv4 traffic on all network interfaces. Reverse path filtering is a security mechanism in Linux that helps prevent IP spoofing and other network attacks. When enabled, it checks if the source IP address of an incoming packet is reachable through the same network interface it was received on. If the packet's source address is not reachable through the interface it arrived on, the packet is dropped. Note: If this system is a router, and uses asymmetrical routing, this recommendation is not applicable.

It is a way of allowing an outside routing device to update your system routing tables. net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_redirects controls accepting of all IPv6 ICMP redirected packets on a newly added network interface. Note: If IPv6 has been disabled, or this system is a router, this recommendation is not applicable.

title: Ensure access to /etc/ssh/sshd_config is configured
description: The file /etc/ssh/sshd_config, and files ending in .conf in the /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d directory, contain configuration specifications for sshd.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=()
   perm_mask='"'"'0177'"'"' && maxperm="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$perm_mask)) )"
   f_sshd_files_chk()
   {
      while IFS=: read -r l_mode l_user l_group; do
         a_out2=()
         [ $(( $l_mode & $perm_mask )) -gt 0 ] && a_out2+=("    Is mode: \"$l_mode\"" \
         "    should be mode: \"$maxperm\" or more restrictive")
         [ "$l_user" != "root" ] && a_out2+=("    Is owned by \"$l_user\" should be owned by \"root\"")
         [ "$l_group" != "root" ] && a_out2+=("    Is group owned by \"$l_user\" should be group owned by \"root\"")
         if [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt "0" ]; then
            a_output2+=("  - File: \"$l_file\":" "${a_out2[@]}")
         else
            a_output+=("  - File: \"$l_file\":" "    Correct: mode ($l_mode), owner ($l_user)" \
            "    and group owner ($l_group) configured")
         fi
      done < <(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a:%U:%G'"'"' "$l_file")
   }
   [ -e "/etc/ssh/sshd_config" ] && l_file="/etc/ssh/sshd_config" && f_sshd_files_chk
   while IFS= read -r -d $'"'"'\0'"'"' l_file; do
      [ -e "$l_file" ] && f_sshd_files_chk
   done < <(find /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d -type f -name '"'"'*.conf'"'"' \( -perm /077 -o ! -user root -o ! -group root \) -print0 2>/dev/null)
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}" ""
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following script to set ownership and permissions on /etc/ssh/sshd_config and files ending in .conf in the /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d directory: #!/usr/bin/env bash { chmod u-x,og-rwx /etc/ssh/sshd_config chown root:root /etc/ssh/sshd_config while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do if [ -e "$l_file" ]; then chmod u-x,og-rwx "$l_file" chown root:root "$l_file" fi done < <(find /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d -type f -print0 2>/dev/null) } - IF - other locations are listed in an Include statement, *.conf files in these locations access should also be modified.

title: Ensure access to SSH public host key files is configured
description: An SSH public key is one of two files used in SSH public key authentication.    l_pmask="0133"; l_maxperm="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"
   f_file_chk()
   {
      while IFS=: read -r l_file_mode l_file_owner l_file_group; do
         a_out2=()
         if [ $(( $l_file_mode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ]; then
            a_out2+=("    Mode: \"$l_file_mode\" should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive")
         fi
         if [ "$l_file_owner" != "root" ]; then
            a_out2+=("    Owned by: \"$l_file_owner\" should be owned by: \"root\"")
         fi
         if [ "$l_file_group" != "root" ]; then
            a_out2+=("    Owned by group \"$l_file_group\" should be group owned by group: \"root\"")
         fi

            [ "$l_fown" != "root" ] && l_output2="$l_output2\n - Directory: \"$l_path\" is owned by: \"$l_fown\" should be owned by \"root\""
            [ $(( $l_fmode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ] && l_output2="$l_output2\n - Directory: \"$l_path\" is mode: \"$l_fmode\" and should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive"

title: Ensure root user umask is configured
description: The user file-creation mode mask (umask) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (rwxrwxrwx), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (rw-rw- rw-). The umask modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The umask is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the umask are cleared in the resulting file mode. umask can be set with either Octal or Symbolic values: • Octal (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four

remediation.guidance: Edit /root/.bash_profile and /root/.bashrc and either: • remove, comment out, or update any line with umask. - OR - • update any line that includes umask to a value of 0027 or more restrictive. Example: umask 027 Note: the Recommendation "Ensure default user umask is configured" includes guidance to set the default umask

      else

      fi
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_export" ]; then
         a_out+=("  - Export is set as: \"$l_tmout_export\" in: \"$l_file\"")
      else
         a_out2+=("  - Export is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
      fi
   }

      l_tmout_value="$(grep -Po -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT=\d+\b'"'"' "$l_file" | awk -F= '"'"'{print $2}'"'"')"
      f_tmout_read_chk
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_value" ]; then

            a_output+=(" - TMOUT is set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")

            [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out[@]}")

      line="umask 027"; ch=1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$t"
  done < "$f"

N=900
# one authoritative file; any other TMOUT assignment is commented out (audit demands readonly+export in each file mentioning it)
for f in /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile.d/*.sh; do

  [ "$f" = /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh ] && continue
  grep -Eq '^[^#]*\bTMOUT\b' "$f" || continue
  tma_bak "$f"; sed -i -E '/^[[:space:]]*#/! s/^([^#]*\bTMOUT\b.*)$/# tmaegis: \1/' "$f"

printf '# CIS: idle shell timeout\nTMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
for f in /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile; do [ -f "$f" ] && ! grep -q '^TMOUT=' "$f" && [ "$f" = /etc/bash/bashrc ] && printf 'TMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" >> "$f"; done

remediation.guidance: First ensure that systemd is correctly configured to ensure that /tmp will be mounted at boot time. # systemctl unmask tmp.mount For specific configuration requirements of the /tmp mount for your environment, modify /etc/fstab. The source location of the volume or disk will vary depending on your environment: <device> /tmp <fstype> defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec 0 0

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=() a_output2=()
   file_access_chk()
   {
      a_out=() a_out2=()
      [[ "$(dirname "$l_file")" =~ ^\/boot\/efi\/EFI ]] && l_pmask="0077" || l_pmask="0177"

title: Ensure /etc/motd is configured
description: The contents of the /etc/motd file are displayed to users after login and function as a message of the day for authenticated users. title: Ensure mail transfer agents are configured for local-only mode
description: Mail Transfer Agents (MTA), such as sendmail and Postfix, are used to listen for incoming mail and transfer the messages to the appropriate user or mail server. If the system is not intended to be a mail server, it is recommended that the MTA be configured to only process local mail.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 Benchmark v4.0.0 - 2.1.23

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=(); a_port_list=("25" "465" "587")
   for l_port_number in "${a_port_list[@]}"; do
      if ss -plntu | grep -P -- '"'"':'"'"'"$l_port_number"'"'"'\b'"'"' | grep -Pvq -- '"'"'\h+(127\.0\.0\.1|\[?::1\]?):'"'"'"$l_port_number"'"'"'\b'"'"'; then
         a_output2+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is listening on a non- loopback network interface")
      else
         a_output+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is not listening on a non- loopback network interface")
      fi
   done
   if command -v postconf &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(postconf -n inet_interfaces)"
   elif command -v exim &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(exim -bP local_interfaces)"
   elif command -v sendmail &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(grep -i "O DaemonPortOptions=" /etc/mail/sendmail.cf | grep -oP '"'"'(?<=Addr=)[^,+]+'"'"' | grep -v '"'"'^127\.0\.0\.1$'"'"')"
   fi
   if [ -n "$l_interfaces" ]; then
      if grep -Pqi '"'"'\ball\b'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to all network interfaces")
      elif ! grep -Pqi '"'"'(inet_interfaces\h*=\h*)?(0\.0\.0\.0|::1|loopback- only|localhost)'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to a network interface" " \"$l_interfaces\"")
      else
         a_output+=(" - MTA is not bound to a non loopback network interface" "   \"$l_interfaces\"")
      fi
   else
      a_output+=(" - MTA not detected or in use")
   fi
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"
      exit "${XCCDF_RESULT_PASS:-101}"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"
      exit "${XCCDF_RESULT_FAIL:-102}"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

If this is the case consult the documentation for your installed MTA to configure the recommended state.

Unload and disable the tipc kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the tipc kernel module: # modprobe -r tipc 2>/dev/null # rmmod tipc 2>/dev/null 2. %s
' "install tipc /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-tipc.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist tipc in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '
%s
' "blacklist tipc" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-tipc.conf

title: Ensure net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter is configured
description: net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter controls reverse path filtering for IPv4 traffic on all network interfaces. Reverse path filtering is a security mechanism in Linux that helps prevent IP spoofing and other network attacks. title: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured
description: TMOUT is an environmental setting that determines the timeout of a shell in seconds. • TMOUT=n - Sets the shell timeout to n seconds. A setting of TMOUT=0 disables timeout. • readonly TMOUT- Sets the TMOUT environmental variable as readonly, preventing unwanted modification during run-time. • export TMOUT - exports the TMOUT variable System Wide Shell Configuration Files: • /etc/profile - used to set system wide environmental variables on users shells. The variables are sometimes the same ones that are in the .bash_profile, however this file is used to set an initial PATH or PS1 for all shell
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 Benchmark v4.0.0 - 5.4.3.2

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=(); l_tmout_set="900"
   f_tmout_read_chk()
   {
      a_out=(); a_out2=()
      l_tmout_readonly="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\- xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\breadonly\h+TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
      l_tmout_export="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\- xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\bexport\b([^#\n\r]+\b)?TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_readonly" ]; then
         a_out+=("  - Readonly is set as: \"$l_tmout_readonly\" in: \"$l_file\"")
      else
         a_out2+=("  - Readonly is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
      fi
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_export" ]; then
         a_out+=("  - Export is set as: \"$l_tmout_export\" in: \"$l_file\"")
      else
         a_out2+=("  - Export is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
      fi
   }
   while IFS= read -r l_file; do
      l_tmout_value="$(grep -Po -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT=\d+\b'"'"' "$l_file" | awk -F= '"'"'{print $2}'"'"')"
      f_tmout_read_chk
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_value" ]; then
         if [[ "$l_tmout_value" -le "$l_tmout_set" && "$l_tmout_value" -gt "0" ]]; then
            a_output+=(" - TMOUT is set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")
            [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output+=("${a_out[@]}")
            [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out[@]}")
         fi
         if [[ "$l_tmout_value" -gt "$l_tmout_set" || "$l_tmout_value" -le "0" ]]; then
            a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is incorrectly set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")
            [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("  ** Incorrect TMOUT value **" "${a_out[@]}")
            [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out2[@]}")
         fi
      else
         [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] &&  a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not set" "${a_out[@]}")
         [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] &&  a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not set" "${a_out2[@]}")
      fi
   done < <(grep -Pls -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT\b'"'"' /etc/*bashrc /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/*.sh)
   [[ "${#a_output[@]}" -le 0 && "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]] && a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not configured")
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_ts=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$tma_ts"; }
tma_applied() { return 0; }

# make every umask line in the given files at least 027
tma_umask_fix() { for f in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  grep -Eqi '^[[:space:]]*umask[[:space:]]' "$f" || continue
  t=$(mktemp); ch=0
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    if [[ $line =~ ^([[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+)0*([0-7]{1,4})([[:space:]#].*)?$ ]]; then
      v=$((8#${BASH_REMATCH[2]})); n=$((v | 8#027))
      if [ "$n" != "$v" ]; then line="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}$(printf '%03o' $n)${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"; ch=1; fi
    elif [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+[ugoa]*= ]] && [[ $line =~ (g=[rwx]*w|o=[rwx]*[rwx]) ]]; then
      line="umask 027"; ch=1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$t"
  done < "$f"
  if [ $ch = 1 ]; then tma_bak "$f"; cat "$t" > "$f"; fi
  rm -f "$t"
done; }
N=900
# one authoritative file; any other TMOUT assignment is commented out (audit demands readonly+export in each file mentioning it)
for f in /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile.d/*.sh; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  [ "$f" = /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh ] && continue
  grep -Eq '^[^#]*\bTMOUT\b' "$f" || continue
  tma_bak "$f"; sed -i -E '/^[[:space:]]*#/! s/^([^#]*\bTMOUT\b.*)$/# tmaegis: \1/' "$f"
done
mkdir -p /etc/profile.d
printf '# CIS: idle shell timeout\nTMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
for f in /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile; do [ -f "$f" ] && ! grep -q '^TMOUT=' "$f" && [ "$f" = /etc/bash/bashrc ] && printf 'TMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" >> "$f"; done
true
remediation.guidance: Review /etc/bashrc, /etc/profile, and all files ending in *.sh in the /etc/profile.d/ directory and remove or edit all TMOUT=_n_ entries to follow local site policy. TMOUT should not exceed 900 or be equal to 0. Configure TMOUT in one of the following files: • A file in the /etc/profile.d/ directory ending in .sh • /etc/profile • /etc/bashrc Example command to set TMOUT to 900 seconds in a file in /etc/profile.d/: # printf '%s\n' "# Set TMOUT to 900 seconds" "typeset -xr TMOUT=900" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmout.sh TMOUT configuration examples: typeset -xr TMOUT=900 Deprecated methods: • As multiple lines: TMOUT=900 readonly TMOUT export TMOUT • As a single line: readonly TMOUT=900 ; export TMOUT

title: Ensure cryptographic mechanisms are used to protect the integrity of audit tools
description: Audit tools include, but are not limited to, vendor-provided and open source audit tools needed to successfully view and manipulate audit information system activity and records. Audit tools include custom queries and report generators.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 Benchmark v4.0.0 - 6.1.3

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=();a_output2=();a_output3=();a_parlist=()

   a_audit_files=("auditctl" "auditd" "ausearch" "aureport" "autrace" "augenrules")

      for l_tool_file in "${a_parlist[@]}"; do

            for l_string in "${!A_out[@]}"; do
               l_check="$(grep -Po -- '"'"'^\h*(\/usr)?\/sbin\/'"'"'"$l_tool_file"'"'"'\b'"'"' <<< "$l_string")"
               if [ -n "$l_check" ]; then
                  l_fname="$(printf '"'"'%s'"'"' "${A_out[$l_string]}")"
                  [ "$l_check" != "$(readlink -f "$l_check")" ] && \
                  a_output3+=("  - \"$l_check\" should be updated to: \"$(readlink -f "$l_check")\"" "    in: \"$l_fname\"")
                  a_missing=()
                  for l_var in "${a_items[@]}"; do
                     if ! grep -Pq -- "\b$l_var\b" <<< "$l_string"; then
                        a_missing+=("\"$l_var\"")
                     fi
                  done
                  if [ "${#a_missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
                     a_output2+=(" - Option(s): ( ${a_missing[*]} ) are missing from: \"$l_tool_file\" in: \"$l_fname\"")
                  else
                     a_output+=(" - Audit tool file \"$l_tool_file\" exists as:" "   \"$l_string\"" "   in the configuration file: \"$l_fname\"")
                  fi
               fi
            done
         else
            a_output2+=(" - Audit tool file \"$l_tool_file\" doesn'"'"'t exist in an AIDE configuration file")
         fi
      done
   }
   f_aide_conf()
   {
      l_config_file="$(whereis aide.conf | awk '"'"'{print $2}'"'"')"
      if [ -f "$l_config_file" ]; then
         a_items=("p" "i" "n" "u" "g" "s" "b" "acl" "xattrs" "sha512")

         while IFS= read -r l_out; do
            if grep -Pq -- '"'"'^\h*\#\h*\/[^#\n\r]+\.conf\b'"'"' <<< "$l_out"; then
               l_file="${l_out//# /}"
            else

            fi

         if [ "${#A_out[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            f_parameter_chk
         else
            a_output2+=(" - No audit tool files are configured in an AIDE configuration file")
         fi
      else
         a_output2+=(" - AIDE configuration file not found." "   Please verify AIDE is installed on the system")
      fi
   }
   for l_audit_file in "${a_audit_files[@]}"; do
      if [ -f "$(readlink -f "/sbin/$l_audit_file")" ]; then
         a_parlist+=("$l_audit_file")
      else
         a_output+=(" - Audit tool file \"$(readlink -f "/sbin/$l_audit_file")\" doesn'"'"'t exist")
      fi
   done
   [ "${#a_parlist[@]}" -gt 0 ] && f_aide_conf
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"
      [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "  ** WARNING **" "${a_output3[@]}"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "  ** WARNING **" "${a_output3[@]}"
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"

}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure SELinux is not disabled in bootloader configuration
description: Configure SELINUX to be enabled at boot time and verify that it has not been overwritten by the grub boot parameters.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 1.3.1.2

audit.command: alt0() { o=$(bash -c 'grubby --info=ALL | grep -Po '"'"'(selinux|enforcing)=0\b'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Prs -- '"'"'^\h*([^#\n\r]+\h+)?kernelopts=([^#\n\r]+\h+)?(selinux|enforcing)=0\b'"'"' /boot/grub2 /boot/efi' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step2: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure the MCS Translation Service (mcstrans) is not installed
description: The mcstransd daemon provides category label information to client processes requesting information. The label translations are defined in /etc/selinux/targeted/setrans.conf
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 1.3.1.7

audit.command: alt0() { command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: rpm not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'rpm -q mcstrans' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'package mcstrans is not installed' || { echo step1: missing 'package mcstrans is not installed'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to uninstall mcstrans: # dnf remove mcstrans

title: Ensure SETroubleshoot is not installed

title: Ensure systemd ability to spawn an interactive boot process is disabled
description: The systemd.confirm_spawn kernel argument causes systemd to prompt interactively at the console before spawning each unit during boot. Removing this argument prevents an interactive boot process.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 1.4.5

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grubby not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grubby --info=ALL | grep -E '"'"'^\s*args='"'"' | grep '"'"'systemd.confirm_spawn'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to remove the systemd.confirm_spawn argument from all boot entries: # grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args=systemd.confirm_spawn Then edit /etc/default/grub and remove systemd.confirm_spawn from the GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX (and GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT) line so it is not reintroduced on the next kernel or bootloader update. If the system uses /etc/kernel/cmdline, remove it there as well.

title: Ensure GDM disable-user-list is configured
description: GNOME Display Manager (GDM) handles graphical login for GNOME based systems. The disable-user-list option controls if a list of users is displayed on the login screen By using the lockdown mode in dconf, you can prevent users from changing specific settings.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 1.8.2

audit.command: alt0() { command -v gsettings >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: gsettings not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'gsettings writable org.gnome.login-screen disable-user-list' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- false || { echo step1: missing false; return 1; }; command -v gsettings >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: gsettings not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'gsettings get org.gnome.login-screen disable-user-list' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- true || { echo step2: missing true; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; return 0; }
tma_ini_set() { # file section key value
  local f=$1 s=$2 k=$3 v=$4
  [ -e "$f" ] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; : > "$f"; }
  tma_bak "$f"
  awk -v s="$s" -v k="$k" -v v="$v" '
    function flush() { if (insec && !done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } }
    /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { flush(); insec = ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*\\[" s "\\][[:space:]]*$"); print; next }
    insec && $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*" k "[[:space:]]*=" { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } ; next }
    { print }
    END { flush(); if (!done) { print "[" s "]"; print k "=" v } }' "$f" > "$f.tma" && cat "$f.tma" > "$f"; rm -f "$f.tma"
}
tma_grub_regen() {
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ -f /boot/grub2/grub.cfg ]; then grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg
    else for c in /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c"; done; fi
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -f /boot/grub/grub.cfg ] && grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
  fi; return 0
}
tma_cmdline_rm() { # names of kernel args (name or name=value) to drop from the grub defaults
  local a f c k n
  for a in "$@"; do
    for f in /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.d/*.cfg; do
      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" "$f" || continue
      tma_bak "$f"
      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"
    done
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args="$a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  if command -v grub2-editenv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    k=$(grub2-editenv - list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^kernelopts=//p')
    if [ -n "$k" ]; then n=$k; for a in "$@"; do n=$(printf '%s' "$n" | sed -E "s/(^| )${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/ /g"); done
      [ "$n" != "$k" ] && grub2-editenv - set "kernelopts=$n"; fi
  fi
  for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/grub/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do
    [ -f "$c" ] || continue
    for a in "$@"; do sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*(linux|kernelopts)/ s/(^|[ =])${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/\1\3/g" "$c"; done
  done
  return 0
}
tma_cmdline_set() { # name=value pairs forced into GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
  local f=/etc/default/grub kv; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $f"; return 0; }
  for kv in "$@"; do
    tma_cmdline_rm "${kv%%=*}" "${kv%%=*}=[^ \"']*" 2>/dev/null
    tma_bak "$f"
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$f"; then
      sed -i -E "s/^([[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=[\"'])(.*)([\"'])\$/\1\2 ${kv}\3/; s/=([\"']) /=\1/" "$f"
    else printf 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="%s"\n' "$kv" >> "$f"; fi
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --args="$kv" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  return 0
}

mkdir -p /etc/dconf/profile /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks
pf() { [ -f "$1" ] || : > "$1"; while IFS= read -r l; do grep -qxF "$l" "$1" || printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$1"; done; }
printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user
system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/$prof

disable-user-list=true
TMAEOF
printf '%s\n' /org/gnome/login-screen/disable-user-list > /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks/00-login-screen
command -v dconf >/dev/null 2>&1 && dconf update
true

title: Ensure bluetooth services are not in use
description: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology standard that is used for exchanging data between devices over short distances. It employs UHF radio waves in the ISM bands, from 2.402 GHz to 2.48 GHz. It is mainly used as an alternative to wire connections.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 3.1.3

audit.command: alt0() { command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: rpm not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'rpm -q bluez' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'package bluez is not installed' || { echo step1: missing 'package bluez is not installed'; return 1; }; }; alt1() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: systemctl not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'systemctl is-enabled bluetooth.service 2>/dev/null | grep '"'"'enabled'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: systemctl not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'systemctl is-active bluetooth.service 2>/dev/null | grep '"'"'^active'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step2: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0 || alt1; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure dccp kernel module is not available
description: The Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP) is a transport layer protocol that supports streaming media and telephony. DCCP provides a way to gain access to congestion control, without having to do it at the application layer, but does not provide in-sequence delivery.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 3.2.1

audit.command: m=dccp; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/dccp*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

Unload and disable the dccp kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the dccp kernel module: # modprobe -r dccp 2>/dev/null # rmmod dccp 2>/dev/null 2. title: Ensure all users last password change date is in the past
description: All users should have a password change date in the past.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.1.6

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
 while IFS= read -r l_user; do
 l_change_raw=$(chage --list "$l_user" | grep '"'"'^Last password change'"'"' | cut - d: -f2 | tr -d '"'"' '"'"')
 [ "$l_change_raw" = "never" ] && continue
 l_change=$(date -u -d "$l_change_raw" +%s 2>/dev/null) || continue
 if [[ "$l_change" -gt "$(date +%s)" ]]; then
 echo "User: \"$l_user\" last password change was \"$l_change_raw\""

Locking the account, expiring the password, or resetting the password manually may be appropriate. title: Ensure root is the only UID 0 account
description: On a Linux system, the user ID (UID) 0 is the superuser identity: the kernel grants any account assigned UID 0 complete, unrestricted control of the host, regardless of the account's name. The root account holds UID 0 by default.

Run the following command to reassign any account other than root that has UID 0 to a new, unused UID (and update ownership of that account's files): # usermod -u <NEW_UID> <username> Example: # usermod -u 1234 bsmith 2. If the root account's UID is not 0, run the following command to reset it: # usermod -u 0 root

title: Ensure root path integrity
description: The PATH variable for the root user determines the directories the shell searches for executables when root runs a command that is not given as an absolute path. Its integrity depends on the ownership, permissions, and composition of the directories it lists.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.2.5

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_pmask="0022"
   l_root_path="$(su - root -c '"'"'printf "%s" "$PATH"'"'"')"
   grep -q  -- "::" <<< "$l_root_path" && echo " - root'"'"'s PATH contains an empty directory (::)"
   grep -Pq -- ":\h*$" <<< "$l_root_path" && echo " - root'"'"'s PATH ends with a trailing colon (:)"
   grep -Pq -- '"'"'(^\h*|:)\.(:|\h*$)'"'"' <<< "$l_root_path" && echo " - root'"'"'s PATH contains the current working directory (.)"
   IFS=":" read -ra a_path_loc <<< "$l_root_path"
   for l_path in "${a_path_loc[@]}"; do
      if [ -d "$l_path" ]; then
         while IFS=: read -r l_fmode l_fown; do
            [ "$l_fown" != "root" ] && echo " - Directory \"$l_path\" is owned by \"$l_fown\" (should be owned by root)"
            [ $(( l_fmode & l_pmask )) -gt 0 ] && echo " - Directory \"$l_path\" is mode \"$l_fmode\" (should be 0755 or more restrictive)"
         done <<< "$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a:%U'"'"' "$l_path")"
      else
         echo " - \"$l_path\" is not an existing directory"
      fi
   done
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

{

description: TMOUT is a shell environment variable that sets an interactive shell's idle timeout, in seconds: after TMOUT seconds with no input, the shell exits.    l_set=0

      l_val="$(grep -Po -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT=\d+\b'"'"' "$l_file" | awk -F= '"'"'{v=$2} END{if (NR>0) print v}'"'"')"

      [ "$l_val" -gt 0 ] && [ "$l_val" -le "$l_max" ] || echo "$l_file: TMOUT=$l_val is out of range (must be >0 and <=$l_max)"

title: Ensure journald service is active
description: systemd-journald is the systemd journaling service that collects and stores system log data. It is a static, socket-activated unit that is always present as the initial collector of log events on a systemd-based system; it is started by systemd rather than enabled to start on boot.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 6.1.1.1

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to unmask and start systemd-journald.service: # systemctl unmask systemd-journald.service # systemctl start systemd-journald.service

title: Ensure access to rsyslog configuration files is configured
description: The main rsyslog configuration file /etc/rsyslog.conf and the drop-in configuration files ending in .conf under /etc/rsyslog.d/ control how rsyslog collects, filters, stores, and forwards system log data. These files should be owned by root, group-owned by root, and no more permissive than mode 0640, so that they can be modified only by root and are not readable by any account other than root.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 6.1.2.4

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to set ownership to root:root and remove group write, all access for other accounts, and all execute bits from the rsyslog configuration files, resulting in mode 0640 or more restrictive: # chown root:root /etc/rsyslog.conf # chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx /etc/rsyslog.conf # find /etc/rsyslog.d/ -type f -name '*.conf' -exec chown root:root {} + # find /etc/rsyslog.d/ -type f -name '*.conf' -exec chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx {} +

title: Ensure access to the /etc/rsyslog.d directory is configured
description: The /etc/rsyslog.d/ directory holds drop-in rsyslog configuration files ending in .conf. The directory should be owned by root, group-owned by root, and not writable by any account other than root so that unauthorized users cannot add, remove, or replace rsyslog configuration fragments.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark v3.0.0 - 6.1.2.5
