title: Ensure all users last password change date is in the past
description: All users should have a password change date in the past.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.1.6

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   while IFS= read -r l_user; do
      l_change=$(date -d "$(chage --list $l_user | grep '"'"'^Last password change'"'"' | cut -d: -f2 | grep -v '"'"'never$'"'"')" +%s)
      if [[ "$l_change" -gt "$(date +%s)" ]]; then
         echo "User: \"$l_user\" last password change was \"$(chage --list $l_user | grep '"'"'^Last password change'"'"' | cut -d: -f2)\""
      fi
   done < <(awk -F: '"'"'$2~/^\$.+\$/{print $1}'"'"' /etc/shadow)
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Investigate any users with a password change date in the future and correct them. Locking the account, expiring the password, or resetting the password manually may be appropriate.

title: Ensure root is the only UID 0 account
description: Any account with UID 0 has superuser privileges on the system.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.2.1

audit.command: alt0() { command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: awk not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'awk -F: '"'"'($3 == 0) { print $1 }'"'"' /etc/passwd' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- root || { echo step1: missing root; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: Run the following command to change the root account UID to 0: # usermod -u 0 root Modify any users other than root with UID 0 and assign them a new UID.

title: Ensure group root is the only GID 0 group
description: The groupmod command can be used to specify which group the root group belongs to. This affects permissions of files that are group owned by the root group.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.2.3

audit.command: alt0() { command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: awk not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'awk -F: '"'"'$3=="0"{print $1":"$3}'"'"' /etc/group' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- root:0 || { echo step1: missing root:0; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: Run the following command to set the root group's GID to 0: # groupmod -g 0 root Remove any groups other than the root group with GID 0 or assign them a new GID if appropriate.

title: Ensure root path integrity
description: The root user can execute any command on the system and could be fooled into executing programs unintentionally if the PATH is not set correctly.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.2.5

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_output2=""
   l_pmask="0022"
   l_maxperm="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"
   l_root_path="$(sudo -Hiu root env | grep '"'"'^PATH'"'"' | cut -d= -f2)"
   unset a_path_loc && IFS=":" read -ra a_path_loc <<< "$l_root_path"
   grep -q "::" <<< "$l_root_path" && l_output2="$l_output2\n - root'"'"'s path contains a empty directory (::)"
   grep -Pq ":\h*$" <<< "$l_root_path" && l_output2="$l_output2\n - root'"'"'s path contains a trailing (:)"
   grep -Pq '"'"'(\h+|:)\.(:|\h*$)'"'"' <<< "$l_root_path" && l_output2="$l_output2\n - root'"'"'s path contains current working directory (.)"
   while read -r l_path; do
      if [ -d "$l_path" ]; then
         while read -r l_fmode l_fown; do
            [ "$l_fown" != "root" ] && l_output2="$l_output2\n - Directory: \"$l_path\" is owned by: \"$l_fown\" should be owned by \"root\""
            [ $(( $l_fmode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ] && l_output2="$l_output2\n - Directory: \"$l_path\" is mode: \"$l_fmode\" and should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive"
         done <<< "$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a %U'"'"' "$l_path")"
      else
         l_output2="$l_output2\n - \"$l_path\" is not a directory"
      fi
   done <<< "$(printf "%s\n" "${a_path_loc[@]}")"
   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  *** PASS ***\n - Root'"'"'s path is correctly configured\n"
   else
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n - * Reasons for audit failure * :\n$l_output2\n"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Correct or justify any: • Locations that are not directories • Empty directories (::) • Trailing (:) • Current working directory (.) • Non root owned directories • Directories that less restrictive than mode 0755

title: Ensure root user umask is configured
description: The user file-creation mode mask (umask) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (rwxrwxrwx), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (rw-rw- rw-). The umask modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The umask is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the umask are cleared in the resulting file mode. umask can be set with either Octal or Symbolic values: • Octal (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.2.6

remediation.guidance: Edit /root/.bash_profile and /root/.bashrc and remove, comment out, or update any line with umask to be 0027 or more restrictive.

title: Ensure accounts without a valid login shell are locked
description: There are a number of accounts provided with most distributions that are used to manage applications and are not intended to provide an interactive shell. Furthermore, a user may add special accounts that are not intended to provide an interactive shell.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.2.8

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_valid_shells="^($(awk -F\/ '"'"'$NF != "nologin" {print}'"'"' /etc/shells | sed -rn '"'"'/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}'"'"' | paste -s -d '"'"'|'"'"' - ))$"
   while IFS= read -r l_user; do
      passwd -S "$l_user" | awk '"'"'$2 !~ /^L/ {print "Account: \"" $1 "\" does not have a valid login shell and is not locked"}'"'"'
   done < <(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '"'"'($1 != "root" && $(NF) !~ pat) {print $1}'"'"' /etc/passwd)
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to lock any non-root accounts without a valid login shell returned by the audit: # usermod -L <user> Example script:: #!/usr/bin/env bash { l_valid_shells="^($(awk -F\/ '$NF != "nologin" {print}' /etc/shells | sed -rn '/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}' | paste -s -d '|' - ))$" while IFS= read -r l_user; do passwd -S "$l_user" | awk '$2 !~ /^L/ {system ("usermod -L " $1)}' done < <(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '($1 != "root" && $(NF) !~ pat) {print $1}' /etc/passwd) }

title: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured
description: TMOUT is an environmental setting that determines the timeout of a shell in seconds. • TMOUT=n - Sets the shell timeout to n seconds. A setting of TMOUT=0 disables timeout. • readonly TMOUT- Sets the TMOUT environmental variable as readonly, preventing unwanted modification during run-time. • export TMOUT - exports the TMOUT variable System Wide Shell Configuration Files: • /etc/profile - used to set system wide environmental variables on users shells. The variables are sometimes the same ones that are in the .bash_profile, however this file is used to set an initial PATH or PS1 for all shell
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 5.4.3.2

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=(); l_tmout_set="900"
   f_tmout_read_chk()
   {
      a_out=(); a_out2=()
      l_tmout_readonly="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\-xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\breadonly\h+TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
      l_tmout_export="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\-xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\bexport\b([^#\n\r]+\b)?TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_readonly" ]; then
         a_out+=("  - Readonly is set as: \"$l_tmout_readonly\" in: \"$l_file\"")
      else
         a_out2+=("  - Readonly is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
      fi
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_export" ]; then
         a_out+=("  - Export is set as: \"$l_tmout_export\" in: \"$l_file\"")
      else
         a_out2+=("  - Export is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
      fi
   }
   while IFS= read -r l_file; do
      l_tmout_value="$(grep -Po -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT=\d+\b'"'"' "$l_file" | awk -F= '"'"'{print $2}'"'"')"
      f_tmout_read_chk
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_value" ]; then
         if [[ "$l_tmout_value" -le "$l_tmout_set" && "$l_tmout_value" -gt "0" ]]; then
            a_output+=(" - TMOUT is set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")
            [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output+=("${a_out[@]}")
            [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out[@]}")
         fi
         if [[ "$l_tmout_value" -gt "$l_tmout_set" || "$l_tmout_value" -le "0" ]]; then
            a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is incorrectly set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")
            [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("  ** Incorrect TMOUT value **" "${a_out[@]}")
            [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out2[@]}")
         fi
      else
         [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] &&  a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not set" "${a_out[@]}")
         [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] &&  a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not set" "${a_out2[@]}")
      fi
   done < <(grep -Pls -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT\b'"'"' /etc/*bashrc /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/*.sh)
   [[ "${#a_output[@]}" -le 0 && "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]] && a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not configured")
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_ts=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$tma_ts"; }
tma_applied() { return 0; }

# make every umask line in the given files at least 027
tma_umask_fix() { for f in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  grep -Eqi '^[[:space:]]*umask[[:space:]]' "$f" || continue
  t=$(mktemp); ch=0
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    if [[ $line =~ ^([[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+)0*([0-7]{1,4})([[:space:]#].*)?$ ]]; then
      v=$((8#${BASH_REMATCH[2]})); n=$((v | 8#027))
      if [ "$n" != "$v" ]; then line="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}$(printf '%03o' $n)${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"; ch=1; fi
    elif [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+[ugoa]*= ]] && [[ $line =~ (g=[rwx]*w|o=[rwx]*[rwx]) ]]; then
      line="umask 027"; ch=1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$t"
  done < "$f"
  if [ $ch = 1 ]; then tma_bak "$f"; cat "$t" > "$f"; fi
  rm -f "$t"
done; }
N=900
# one authoritative file; any other TMOUT assignment is commented out (audit demands readonly+export in each file mentioning it)
for f in /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile.d/*.sh; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  [ "$f" = /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh ] && continue
  grep -Eq '^[^#]*\bTMOUT\b' "$f" || continue
  tma_bak "$f"; sed -i -E '/^[[:space:]]*#/! s/^([^#]*\bTMOUT\b.*)$/# tmaegis: \1/' "$f"
done
mkdir -p /etc/profile.d
printf '# CIS: idle shell timeout\nTMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
for f in /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile; do [ -f "$f" ] && ! grep -q '^TMOUT=' "$f" && [ "$f" = /etc/bash/bashrc ] && printf 'TMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" >> "$f"; done
true
remediation.guidance: Review /etc/bashrc, /etc/profile, and all files ending in *.sh in the /etc/profile.d/ directory and remove or edit all TMOUT=_n_ entries to follow local site policy. TMOUT should not exceed 900 or be equal to 0. Configure TMOUT in one of the following files: • A file in the /etc/profile.d/ directory ending in .sh • /etc/profile • /etc/bashrc Example command to set TMOUT to 900 seconds in a file in /etc/profile.d/: # printf '%s\n' "# Set TMOUT to 900 seconds" "typeset -xr TMOUT=900" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmout.sh TMOUT configuration examples: typeset -xr TMOUT=900 Deprecated methods: • As multiple lines: TMOUT=900 readonly TMOUT export TMOUT • As a single line: readonly TMOUT=900 ; export TMOUT

title: Ensure default user umask is configured
description: The user file-creation mode mask (umask) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (rwxrwxrwx), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (rw-rw- rw-). The umask modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The umask is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the umask are cleared in the resulting file mode. umask can be set with either Octal or Symbolic values: • Octal (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four

       elif grep -Psiq -- '"'"'^\h*umask\h+(([0-7][0-7][01][0-7]\b|[0-7][0-7][0-7][0-6]\b)|([0-7][01][0-7]\b|[0- 7][0-7][0- 6]\b)|(u=[rwx]{1,3},)?(((g=[rx]?[rx]?w[rx]?[rx]?\b)(,o=[rwx]{1,3})?)|((g=[wrx]{1,3},)?o=[wrx]{1,3}\b)))'"'"' "$l_file"; then
          l_output2="$l_output2\n - umask is incorrectly set in \"$l_file\""

    done < <(find /etc/profile.d/ -type f -name '"'"'*.sh'"'"' -print0)
    [ -z "$l_output" ] && l_file="/etc/profile" && file_umask_chk
    [ -z "$l_output" ] && l_file="/etc/bashrc" && file_umask_chk
    [ -z "$l_output" ] && l_file="/etc/bash.bashrc" && file_umask_chk
    [ -z "$l_output" ] && l_file="/etc/pam.d/postlogin"

title: Ensure AIDE is installed

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
TMA_AUDITD_CONF=/etc/audit/auditd.conf
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; }
tma_audit_pkg() {
  command -v auditctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f /etc/audit/auditd.conf ] && return 0
  if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then tma_pkg_install auditd; else tma_pkg_install audit; fi; }
tma_nl() { [ -s "$1" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c1 "$1")" ] && echo >> "$1"; return 0; }
tma_kv() { # file key value : 'key = value' style (auditd.conf); replaces every uncommented line
  f=$1; k=$2; v=$3
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
  tma_bak "$f"
  if grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*$k[[:space:]]*=" "$f"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^[[:space:]]*$k[[:space:]]*=.*|$k = $v|" "$f"
  else tma_nl "$f"; printf '%s = %s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"; fi; }
tma_ini_set() { # file section key value : systemd ini 'Key=value'
  f=$1; s=$2; k=$3; v=$4
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; [ -f "$f" ] || : > "$f"; tma_nl "$f"
  sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*$k[[:space:]]*=/d" "$f"
  if grep -q "^\[$s\]" "$f"; then sed -i "/^\[$s\]/a $k=$v" "$f"; else printf '[%s]\n%s=%s\n' "$s" "$k" "$v" >> "$f"; fi; }
tma_clear() { # path octal-mask : remove the mask bits from the file mode
  [ -e "$1" ] || return 0
  m=$(stat -Lc %a "$1")
  [ $((8#$m & 8#$2)) -eq 0 ] || chmod "$(printf '%o' $((8#$m & ~8#$2 & 8#7777)))" "$1"; }
tma_rule() { # rules.d-filename audit-rule-line : append when missing (whitespace-normalised)
  f=/etc/audit/rules.d/$1; shift; l=$*
  mkdir -p /etc/audit/rules.d; [ -f "$f" ] || : > "$f"
  if ! tr -s ' \t' '  ' < "$f" | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- "$l"; then tma_nl "$f"; printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$f"; fi
  chown root:root "$f"; chmod 640 "$f"; }
tma_rules_load() { command -v augenrules >/dev/null 2>&1 && augenrules --load >/dev/null 2>&1; true; }
tma_audit_logdir() {
  d=$(awk -F= '/^[[:space:]]*log_file[[:space:]]*=/{print $2}' /etc/audit/auditd.conf 2>/dev/null | xargs 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$d" ] && dirname "$d" || echo /var/log/audit; }
tma_grub_arg() { # key=value : add/replace in GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX and regenerate grub.cfg
  a=$1; k=${a%%=*}; g=/etc/default/grub
  [ -f "$g" ] || { echo "no $g: bootloader not managed by grub defaults" >&2; return 0; }
  tma_bak "$g"
  if ! grep -q '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$g"; then tma_nl "$g"; printf 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="%s"\n' "$a" >> "$g"
  elif grep -E '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$g" | grep -Eq "[\"' ]$k(=|[\"' ])"; then
    sed -i -E "/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#([\"' ])$k(=[^\"' ]*)?([\"' ])#\1$a\3#" "$g"
  else
    sed -i -E "/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#([\"'])\$#  $a\1#; /^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#=([\"'])  #=\1#; /^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#   *# #g" "$g"
  fi
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg >/dev/null 2>&1; fi
  true; }
command -v aide >/dev/null 2>&1 || tma_pkg_install aide
sbin=$(readlink -f /sbin)
if [ -f /etc/aide.conf ]; then cf=/etc/aide.conf
elif [ -f /etc/aide/aide.conf ]; then cf=/etc/aide/aide.conf
else echo "AIDE configuration file not found" >&2; exit 0; fi
tma_bak "$cf"
tmp=$cf.tmaegis.new
grep -Ev '^[[:space:]]*(/usr)?/sbin/(auditctl|auditd|ausearch|aureport|autrace|augenrules)[[:space:]]|^# Audit Tools$' "$cf" > "$tmp"
tma_nl "$tmp"
{ echo '# Audit Tools'
  for t in auditctl auditd ausearch aureport autrace augenrules; do
    echo "$sbin/$t p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512"
    [ "$sbin" != /sbin ] && echo "/sbin/$t p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512"
  done; } >> "$tmp"
cat "$tmp" > "$cf"; rm -f "$tmp"; true

alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{

   {

      [[ ! "$l_user" =~ $l_auser ]] && \

                  perm_mask='"'"'0133'"'"' l_auser="(root|syslog)" l_agroup="(root|adm)"

audit.command: m=cramfs; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/cramfs*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Unload and disable the cramfs kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the cramfs kernel module: # modprobe -r cramfs 2>/dev/null # rmmod cramfs 2>/dev/null 2. Perform the following to disable the cramfs kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install cramfs /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory. Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "install cramfs /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60- cramfs.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist cramfs in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory. Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "blacklist cramfs" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-cramfs.conf

title: Ensure /tmp is tmpfs or a separate partition
description: The /tmp directory is a world-writable directory used for temporary storage by all users and some applications. Note: If an entry for /tmp exists in /etc/fstab it will take precedence over entries in a systemd unit file. There is an exception to this when a system is diskless and connected to iSCSI, entries in /etc/fstab may not take precedence over a systemd unit file.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 22.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 1.1.2.1.1

audit.command: if findmnt -kn /tmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo compliant; else echo /tmp' is not a separate partition'; fi

remediation.guidance: First ensure that systemd is correctly configured to ensure that /tmp will be mounted at boot time. # systemctl unmask tmp.mount For specific configuration requirements of the /tmp mount for your environment, modify /etc/fstab. Example of using tmpfs with specific mount options: tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,size=2G 0 0 Note: the size=2G is an example of setting a specific size for tmpfs. Example of using a volume or disk with specific mount options. The source location of the volume or disk will vary depending on your environment: <device> /tmp <fstype> defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec 0 0

title: Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition
description: The nodev mount option specifies that the filesystem cannot contain special devices.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 22.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 1.1.2.1.2

audit.command: if ! findmnt -kn /tmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo compliant; elif findmnt -kn /tmp | grep -qw -- nodev; then echo compliant; else echo /tmp' is mounted without nodev'; fi

remediation.guidance: - IF - a separate partition exists for /tmp. Edit the /etc/fstab file and add nodev to the fourth field (mounting options) for the /tmp partition. Example: <device> /tmp <fstype> defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0 Run the following command to remount /tmp with the configured options: # mount -o remount /tmp

    /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { flush(); insec = ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*\\[" s "\\][[:space:]]*$"); print; next }
    insec && $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*" k "[[:space:]]*=" { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } ; next }
    { print }
    END { flush(); if (!done) { print "[" s "]"; print k "=" v } }' "$f" > "$f.tma" && cat "$f.tma" > "$f"; rm -f "$f.tma"
}
tma_grub_regen() {
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ -f /boot/grub2/grub.cfg ]; then grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg
    else for c in /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c"; done; fi
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -f /boot/grub/grub.cfg ] && grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
  fi; return 0
}
tma_cmdline_rm() { # names of kernel args (name or name=value) to drop from the grub defaults
  local a f c k n
  for a in "$@"; do
    for f in /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.d/*.cfg; do
      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" "$f" || continue
      tma_bak "$f"
      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"
    done
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args="$a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  if command -v grub2-editenv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    k=$(grub2-editenv - list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^kernelopts=//p')
    if [ -n "$k" ]; then n=$k; for a in "$@"; do n=$(printf '%s' "$n" | sed -E "s/(^| )${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/ /g"); done
      [ "$n" != "$k" ] && grub2-editenv - set "kernelopts=$n"; fi
  fi
  for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/grub/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do
    [ -f "$c" ] || continue
    for a in "$@"; do sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*(linux|kernelopts)/ s/(^|[ =])${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/\1\3/g" "$c"; done
  done
  return 0
}
tma_cmdline_set() { # name=value pairs forced into GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
  local f=/etc/default/grub kv; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $f"; return 0; }
  for kv in "$@"; do
    tma_cmdline_rm "${kv%%=*}" "${kv%%=*}=[^ \"']*" 2>/dev/null
    tma_bak "$f"
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$f"; then
      sed -i -E "s/^([[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=[\"'])(.*)([\"'])\$/\1\2 ${kv}\3/; s/=([\"']) /=\1/" "$f"
    else printf 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="%s"\n' "$kv" >> "$f"; fi
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --args="$kv" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  return 0
}

mkdir -p /etc/dconf/profile /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks
pf() { [ -f "$1" ] || : > "$1"; while IFS= read -r l; do grep -qxF "$l" "$1" || printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$1"; done; }
printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user
system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/$prof

autorun-never=true

title: Ensure mail transfer agents are configured for local-only mode
description: Mail Transfer Agents (MTA), such as sendmail and Postfix, are used to listen for incoming mail and transfer the messages to the appropriate user or mail server. If the system is not intended to be a mail server, it is recommended that the MTA be configured to only process local mail.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=(); a_port_list=("25" "465" "587")
   for l_port_number in "${a_port_list[@]}"; do
      if ss -plntu | grep -P -- '"'"':'"'"'"$l_port_number"'"'"'\b'"'"' | grep -Pvq -- '"'"'\h+(127\.0\.0\.1|\[?::1\]?):'"'"'"$l_port_number"'"'"'\b'"'"'; then
         a_output2+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is listening on a non- loopback network interface")
      else
         a_output+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is not listening on a non- loopback network interface")
      fi
   done
   if command -v postconf &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(postconf -n inet_interfaces)"
   elif command -v exim &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(exim -bP local_interfaces)"
   elif command -v sendmail &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(grep -i "O DaemonPortOptions=" /etc/mail/sendmail.cf | grep -oP '"'"'(?<=Addr=)[^,+]+'"'"' | grep -v '"'"'^127\.0\.0\.1$'"'"')"
   fi
   if [ -n "$l_interfaces" ]; then
      if grep -Pqi '"'"'\ball\b'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to all network interfaces")
      elif ! grep -Pqi '"'"'(inet_interfaces\h*=\h*)?(0\.0\.0\.0|::1|loopback- only)'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to a network interface" " \"$l_interfaces\"")
      else
         a_output+=(" - MTA is not bound to a non loopback network interface" "   \"$l_interfaces\"")
      fi
   else
      a_output+=(" - MTA not detected or in use")
   fi
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

            l_out2="$l_out2\n  - Daemon: \"$l_service_name\" is active on the system"
        fi

audit.command: m=dccp; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/dccp*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance:
Unload and disable the dccp kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the dccp kernel module: # modprobe -r dccp 2>/dev/null # rmmod dccp 2>/dev/null 2. Perform the following to disable the dccp kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install dccp /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '
%s
' "install dccp /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-dccp.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist dccp in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '
%s
' "blacklist dccp" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-dccp.conf

title: Ensure net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter is configured
description: net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter controls reverse path filtering for IPv4 traffic on all network interfaces. Reverse path filtering is a security mechanism in Linux that helps prevent IP spoofing and other network attacks. title: Ensure root user umask is configured
description: The user file-creation mode mask (umask) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (rwxrwxrwx), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (rw-rw- rw-). The umask modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The umask is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the umask are cleared in the resulting file mode. umask can be set with either Octal or Symbolic values: • Octal (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four

title: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured

The variables are sometimes the same ones that are in the .bash_profile, however this file is used to set an initial PATH or PS1 for all shell

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{

      if [ -n "$l_tmout_readonly" ]; then

            [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output+=("${a_out[@]}")

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_ts=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$tma_ts"; }
tma_applied() { return 0; }

# make every umask line in the given files at least 027
tma_umask_fix() { for f in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  grep -Eqi '^[[:space:]]*umask[[:space:]]' "$f" || continue
  t=$(mktemp); ch=0
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    if [[ $line =~ ^([[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+)0*([0-7]{1,4})([[:space:]#].*)?$ ]]; then
      v=$((8#${BASH_REMATCH[2]})); n=$((v | 8#027))
      if [ "$n" != "$v" ]; then line="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}$(printf '%03o' $n)${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"; ch=1; fi
    elif [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+[ugoa]*= ]] && [[ $line =~ (g=[rwx]*w|o=[rwx]*[rwx]) ]]; then
      line="umask 027"; ch=1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$t"
  done < "$f"
  if [ $ch = 1 ]; then tma_bak "$f"; cat "$t" > "$f"; fi
  rm -f "$t"
done; }
N=900
# one authoritative file; any other TMOUT assignment is commented out (audit demands readonly+export in each file mentioning it)
for f in /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile.d/*.sh; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  [ "$f" = /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh ] && continue
  grep -Eq '^[^#]*\bTMOUT\b' "$f" || continue
  tma_bak "$f"; sed -i -E '/^[[:space:]]*#/! s/^([^#]*\bTMOUT\b.*)$/# tmaegis: \1/' "$f"
done
mkdir -p /etc/profile.d
printf '# CIS: idle shell timeout\nTMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
for f in /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile; do [ -f "$f" ] && ! grep -q '^TMOUT=' "$f" && [ "$f" = /etc/bash/bashrc ] && printf 'TMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" >> "$f"; done
true
remediation.guidance: Review /etc/bashrc, /etc/profile, and all files ending in *.sh in the /etc/profile.d/ directory and remove or edit all TMOUT=_n_ entries to follow local site policy. TMOUT should not exceed 900 or be equal to 0. Configure TMOUT in one of the following files: • A file in the /etc/profile.d/ directory ending in .sh • /etc/profile • /etc/bashrc Example command to set TMOUT to 900 seconds in a file in /etc/profile.d/: # printf '%s\n' "# Set TMOUT to 900 seconds" "typeset -xr TMOUT=900" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmout.sh TMOUT configuration examples: typeset -xr TMOUT=900 Deprecated methods: • As multiple lines: TMOUT=900 readonly TMOUT export TMOUT • As a single line: readonly TMOUT=900 ; export TMOUT

audit.command: m=cramfs; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/cramfs*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Unload and disable the cramfs kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the cramfs kernel module: # modprobe -r cramfs 2>/dev/null # rmmod cramfs 2>/dev/null 2. Perform the following to disable the cramfs kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install cramfs /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory. Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "install cramfs /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60- cramfs.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist cramfs in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory. title: Ensure /tmp is tmpfs or a separate partition
description: The /tmp directory is a world-writable directory used for temporary storage by all users and some applications. Note: If an entry for /tmp exists in /etc/fstab it will take precedence over entries in a systemd unit file. There is an exception to this when a system is diskless and connected to iSCSI, entries in /etc/fstab may not take precedence over a systemd unit file.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.1.2.1.1

audit.command: if findmnt -kn /tmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo compliant; else echo /tmp' is not a separate partition'; fi

remediation.guidance: First ensure that systemd is correctly configured to ensure that /tmp will be mounted at boot time. # systemctl unmask tmp.mount For specific configuration requirements of the /tmp mount for your environment, modify /etc/fstab. Example of using tmpfs with specific mount options: tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,size=2G 0 0 Note: the size=2G is an example of setting a specific size for tmpfs. Example of using a volume or disk with specific mount options. The source location of the volume or disk will vary depending on your environment: <device> /tmp <fstype> defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec 0 0 Note: Using Btrfs subvolumes instead of traditional disk partitions changes ho…

title: Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition
description: The nodev mount option specifies that the filesystem cannot contain special devices.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.1.2.1.2

audit.command: if ! findmnt -kn /tmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo compliant; elif findmnt -kn /tmp | grep -qw -- nodev; then echo compliant; else echo /tmp' is mounted without nodev'; fi

remediation.guidance: - IF - a separate partition exists for /tmp. Edit the /etc/fstab file and add nodev to the fourth field (mounting options) for the /tmp partition. Example: <device> /tmp <fstype> defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0 Run the following command to remount /tmp with the configured options: # mount -o remount /tmp

title: Ensure access to gpg key files are configured
description: GPG key files are cryptographic keys used by APT to verify the authenticity and integrity of software packages. Each key ensures that packages come from a trusted source and have not been tampered with. These keys are typically stored in keyring directories /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d or /usr/share/keyrings and referenced in repository configuration files using the signed-by option for secure package verification.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.2.1.3

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   while IFS= read -r -d $'"'"'\0'"'"' l_file; do
      grep -PRiLs -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bSigned-By\b'"'"' "$l_file" && \
      stat -Lc '"'"'File: %n Mode: (%#a) User: (%U) Group: (%G)'"'"' "$l_file"
   done < <(find -L /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ -mount -xdev -type f \
   \( ! -user root -o ! -group root -o -perm /133 \) \
   \( -name '"'"'*.list'"'"' -o -name '"'"'*.sources'"'"' \) -print0)
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: Run the following commands to update the access to any file(s) returned in the audit steps above: # chown root:root "/absolute/path/to/file" # chmod u-x,go-wx "/absolute/path/to/file" Example # chown root:root /usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-trixie-security- automatic.gpg # chmod u-x,go-wx /usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-trixie-security- automatic.gpg Note: APT first checks keys specified with the signed-by option in a repository's .sources or .list files. If no key is specified there, it falls back to administrator- managed keyrings in /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d, then system-wide keyrings in /usr/share/keyrings.

title: Ensure GDM disable-user-list is configured
description: GNOME Display Manager (GDM) handles graphical login for GNOME based systems. The disable-user-list option controls if a list of users is displayed on the login screen By using the lockdown mode in dconf, you can prevent users from changing specific settings.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.7.2

audit.command: alt0() { command -v gsettings >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: gsettings not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'gsettings writable org.gnome.login-screen disable-user-list' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- false || { echo step1: missing false; return 1; }; command -v gsettings >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: gsettings not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'gsettings get org.gnome.login-screen disable-user-list' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- true || { echo step2: missing true; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; return 0; }
tma_ini_set() { # file section key value
  local f=$1 s=$2 k=$3 v=$4
  [ -e "$f" ] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; : > "$f"; }
  tma_bak "$f"
  awk -v s="$s" -v k="$k" -v v="$v" '
    function flush() { if (insec && !done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } }
    /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { flush(); insec = ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*\\[" s "\\][[:space:]]*$"); print; next }
    insec && $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*" k "[[:space:]]*=" { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } ; next }
    { print }
    END { flush(); if (!done) { print "[" s "]"; print k "=" v } }' "$f" > "$f.tma" && cat "$f.tma" > "$f"; rm -f "$f.tma"
}
tma_grub_regen() {
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ -f /boot/grub2/grub.cfg ]; then grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg
    else for c in /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c"; done; fi
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -f /boot/grub/grub.cfg ] && grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
  fi; return 0
}
tma_cmdline_rm() { # names of kernel args (name or name=value) to drop from the grub defaults
  local a f c k n
  for a in "$@"; do
    for f in /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.d/*.cfg; do
      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" "$f" || continue
      tma_bak "$f"
      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"
    done
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args="$a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  if command -v grub2-editenv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    k=$(grub2-editenv - list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^kernelopts=//p')
    if [ -n "$k" ]; then n=$k; for a in "$@"; do n=$(printf '%s' "$n" | sed -E "s/(^| )${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/ /g"); done
      [ "$n" != "$k" ] && grub2-editenv - set "kernelopts=$n"; fi
  fi
  for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/grub/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do
    [ -f "$c" ] || continue
    for a in "$@"; do sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*(linux|kernelopts)/ s/(^|[ =])${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/\1\3/g" "$c"; done
  done
  return 0
}
tma_cmdline_set() { # name=value pairs forced into GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
  local f=/etc/default/grub kv; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $f"; return 0; }
  for kv in "$@"; do
    tma_cmdline_rm "${kv%%=*}" "${kv%%=*}=[^ \"']*" 2>/dev/null
    tma_bak "$f"
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$f"; then
      sed -i -E "s/^([[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=[\"'])(.*)([\"'])\$/\1\2 ${kv}\3/; s/=([\"']) /=\1/" "$f"

  done
  return 0
}

mkdir -p /etc/dconf/profile /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks

printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user
system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/$prof

[org/gnome/login-screen]
disable-user-list=true
TMAEOF
printf '%s\n' /org/gnome/login-screen/disable-user-list > /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks/00-login-screen
command -v dconf >/dev/null 2>&1 && dconf update
true

      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" "$f" || continue
      tma_bak "$f"
      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"
    done
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args="$a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  if command -v grub2-editenv >/dev/null 2>&1; then

    if [ -n "$k" ]; then n=$k; for a in "$@"; do n=$(printf '%s' "$n" | sed -E "s/(^| )${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/ /g"); done

  fi

    for a in "$@"; do sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*(linux|kernelopts)/ s/(^|[ =])${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/\1\3/g" "$c"; done
  done
  return 0
}

alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{

      fi
   done

      l_interfaces="$(postconf -n inet_interfaces)"
   elif command -v exim &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(exim -bP local_interfaces)"
   elif command -v sendmail &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(grep -i "O DaemonPortOptions=" /etc/mail/sendmail.cf | grep -oP '"'"'(?<=Addr=)[^,+]+'"'"' | grep -v '"'"'^127\.0\.0\.1$'"'"')"
   fi
   if [ -n "$l_interfaces" ]; then

      elif ! grep -Pqi '"'"'(inet_interfaces\h*=\h*)?(0\.0\.0\.0|::1|loopback- only)'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to a network interface" " \"$l_interfaces\"")
      else
         a_output+=(" - MTA is not bound to a non loopback network interface" "   \"$l_interfaces\"")
      fi
   else
      a_output+=(" - MTA not detected or in use")
   fi
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"

      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""

audit.command:

{
   l_output="" l_output2=""
   module_chk()
   {
      # Check how module will be loaded
      l_loadable="$(modprobe -n -v "$l_mname")"
      if grep -Pq -- '"'"'^\h*install \/bin\/(true|false)'"'"' <<< "$l_loadable"; then
         l_output="$l_output\n - module: \"$l_mname\" is not loadable: \"$l_loadable\""
      else
         l_output2="$l_output2\n - module: \"$l_mname\" is loadable: \"$l_loadable\""
      fi
      # Check is the module currently loaded
      if ! lsmod | grep "$l_mname" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
         l_output="$l_output\n - module: \"$l_mname\" is not loaded"
      else
         l_output2="$l_output2\n - module: \"$l_mname\" is loaded"
      fi
      # Check if the module is deny listed
      if modprobe --showconfig | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+$l_mname\b"; then
         l_output="$l_output\n - module: \"$l_mname\" is deny listed in: \"$(grep -Pl -- "^\h*blacklist\h+$l_mname\b" /etc/modprobe.d/*)\""
      else
         l_output2="$l_output2\n - module: \"$l_mname\" is not deny listed"
      fi
   }
   if [ -n "$(find /sys/class/net/*/ -type d -name wireless)" ]; then
      l_dname=$(for driverdir in $(find /sys/class/net/*/ -type d -name wireless | xargs -0 dirname); do basename "$(readlink -f "$driverdir"/device/driver/module)";done | sort -u)
      for l_mname in $l_dname; do
         module_chk
      done
   fi

   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** PASS **"
      if [ -z "$l_output" ]; then
         echo -e "\n - System has no wireless NICs installed"
      else
         echo -e "\n$l_output\n"
      fi
   else
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n - Reason(s) for audit failure:\n$l_output2\n"
      [ -n "$l_output" ] && echo -e "\n- Correctly set:\n$l_output\n"
   fi

title: Ensure atm kernel module is not available
description: The Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) is a protocol operating on network, data link, and physical layers, based on virtual circuits and virtual paths. Disabling ATM protects the system against exploitation of any laws in its implementation.

description: The root user can execute any command on the system and could be fooled into executing programs unintentionally if the PATH is not set correctly.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.4.2.5

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output2=() l_pmask="0022"
   l_maxperm="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"
   l_root_path="$(sudo su - root -c env | awk -F= '"'"'$1=="PATH"{print $2}'"'"')"
   IFS=":" read -ra a_path_loc <<< "$l_root_path"
   grep -q -- "::" <<< "$l_root_path" && \
   a_output2+=(" - root'"'"'s path contains a empty directory (::)")
   grep -Pq -- ":\h*$" <<< "$l_root_path" && \
   a_output2+=(" - root'"'"'s path contains a trailing (:)")
   grep -Pq -- '"'"'(^\h*|:)\.(:|\h*$)'"'"' <<< "$l_root_path" && \
   a_output2+=(" - root'"'"'s path contains current working directory (.)")
   for l_path in "${a_path_loc[@]}"; do
      if [ -d "$l_path" ]; then
         while IFS=: read -r l_fmode l_fown; do
            [ "$l_fown" != "root" ] && \
            a_output2+=(" - Directory: \"$l_path\" is owned by: \"$l_fown\"" \
            "    should be owned by \"root\"")
            [ $(( $l_fmode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ] && \
            a_output2+=(" - Directory: \"$l_path\" is mode: \"$l_fmode\"" \
            "    and should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive")
         done <<< "$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a:%U'"'"' "$l_path")"
      else
         a_output2+=(" - \"$l_path\" is not a directory")
      fi
   done
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" \
      " - Root'"'"'s path is correctly configured"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" \
      "- * Reasons for audit failure * :" "${a_output2[@]}"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Correct or justify any: • Locations that are not directories • Empty directories (::) • Trailing (:) • Current working directory (.) • Non root owned directories • Directories that less restrictive than mode 0755

title: Ensure root user umask is configured
description: The user file-creation mode mask (umask) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (rwxrwxrwx), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (rw-rw- rw-). The umask modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The umask is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the umask are cleared in the resulting file mode. umask can be set with either Octal or Symbolic values: • Octal (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.4.2.6

audit.command: alt0() { o=$(bash -c 'grep -Psi -- '"'"'^\h*umask\h+((\d{1,2}(\d[^7]|[^2- 7]\d)\b)|(u=[rwx]{1,3},)?(((g=[rx]?[rx]?w[rx]?[rx]?\b)(,o=[rwx]{1,3})?)|((g=[ wrx]{1,3},)?o=[wrx]{1,3}\b)))'"'"' /root/.profile /root/.bashrc' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit /root/.profile and /root/.bashrc and either: • remove, comment out, or update any line with umask. - OR - • update any line that includes umask to a value of 0027 or more restrictive. Example: umask 027 Note: the Recommendation "Ensure default user umask is configured" includes guidance to set the default umask

title: Ensure accounts without a valid login shell are locked
description: There are a number of accounts provided with most distributions that are used to manage applications and are not intended to provide an interactive shell. Furthermore, a user may add special accounts that are not intended to provide an interactive shell.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.4.2.8

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_valid_shells="^($(awk -F\/ '"'"'$NF != "nologin" {print}'"'"' /etc/shells | sed -rn '"'"'/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}'"'"' | paste -s -d '"'"'|'"'"' - ))$"
   while IFS= read -r l_user; do
      passwd -S "$l_user" | awk '"'"'$2 !~ /^L/ {print "Account: \"" $1 "\" does not have a valid login shell and is not locked"}'"'"'
   done < <(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '"'"'($1 != "root" && $(NF) !~ pat) {print $1}'"'"' /etc/passwd)
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to lock any non-root accounts without a valid login shell returned by the audit: # usermod -L <user> Example script:: #!/usr/bin/env bash { l_valid_shells="^($(awk -F\/ '$NF != "nologin" {print}' /etc/shells | sed -rn '/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}' | paste -s -d '|' - ))$" while IFS= read -r l_user; do passwd -S "$l_user" | awk '$2 !~ /^L/ {system ("usermod -L " $1)}' done < <(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '($1 != "root" && $(NF) !~ pat) {print $1}' /etc/passwd) }

title: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured
description: TMOUT is an environmental setting that determines the timeout of a shell in seconds. • TMOUT=n - Sets the shell timeout to n seconds. A setting of TMOUT=0 disables timeout. • readonly TMOUT- Sets the TMOUT environmental variable as readonly, preventing unwanted modification during run-time. • export TMOUT - exports the TMOUT variable System Wide Shell Configuration Files: • /etc/profile - used to set system wide environmental variables on users shells. The variables are sometimes the same ones that are in the .bash_profile, however this file is used to set an initial PATH or PS1 for all shell
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.4.3.2

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=(); l_tmout_set="900"
   f_tmout_read_chk()
   {
      a_out=(); a_out2=()
      l_tmout_readonly="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\- xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\breadonly\h+TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
      l_tmout_export="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\- xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\bexport\b([^#\n\r]+\b)?TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_readonly" ]; then
         a_out+=("  - Readonly is set as: \"$l_tmout_readonly\" in: \"$l_file\"")
      else
         a_out2+=("  - Readonly is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
      fi
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_export" ]; then
         a_out+=("  - Export is set as: \"$l_tmout_export\" in: \"$l_file\"")
      else
         a_out2+=("  - Export is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
      fi
   }
   while IFS= read -r l_file; do
      l_tmout_value="$(grep -Po -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT=\d+\b'"'"' "$l_file" | awk -F= '"'"'{print $2}'"'"')"
      f_tmout_read_chk
      if [ -n "$l_tmout_value" ]; then
         if [[ "$l_tmout_value" -le "$l_tmout_set" && "$l_tmout_value" -gt "0" ]]; then
            a_output+=(" - TMOUT is set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")
            [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output+=("${a_out[@]}")
            [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out[@]}")
         fi
         if [[ "$l_tmout_value" -gt "$l_tmout_set" || "$l_tmout_value" -le "0" ]]; then
            a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is incorrectly set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")
            [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("  ** Incorrect TMOUT value **" "${a_out[@]}")
            [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out2[@]}")
         fi
      else
         [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] &&  a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not set" "${a_out[@]}")
         [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] &&  a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not set" "${a_out2[@]}")
      fi
   done < <(grep -Pls -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT\b'"'"' /etc/*bashrc /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/*.sh)
   [[ "${#a_output[@]}" -le 0 && "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]] && a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not configured")
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_ts=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$tma_ts"; }
tma_applied() { return 0; }

# make every umask line in the given files at least 027
tma_umask_fix() { for f in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  grep -Eqi '^[[:space:]]*umask[[:space:]]' "$f" || continue
  t=$(mktemp); ch=0
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    if [[ $line =~ ^([[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+)0*([0-7]{1,4})([[:space:]#].*)?$ ]]; then
      v=$((8#${BASH_REMATCH[2]})); n=$((v | 8#027))
      if [ "$n" != "$v" ]; then line="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}$(printf '%03o' $n)${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"; ch=1; fi
    elif [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+[ugoa]*= ]] && [[ $line =~ (g=[rwx]*w|o=[rwx]*[rwx]) ]]; then
      line="umask 027"; ch=1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$t"
  done < "$f"
  if [ $ch = 1 ]; then tma_bak "$f"; cat "$t" > "$f"; fi
  rm -f "$t"
done; }
N=900
# one authoritative file; any other TMOUT assignment is commented out (audit demands readonly+export in each file mentioning it)
for f in /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile.d/*.sh; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  [ "$f" = /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh ] && continue
  grep -Eq '^[^#]*\bTMOUT\b' "$f" || continue
  tma_bak "$f"; sed -i -E '/^[[:space:]]*#/! s/^([^#]*\bTMOUT\b.*)$/# tmaegis: \1/' "$f"
done
mkdir -p /etc/profile.d
printf '# CIS: idle shell timeout\nTMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
for f in /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile; do [ -f "$f" ] && ! grep -q '^TMOUT=' "$f" && [ "$f" = /etc/bash/bashrc ] && printf 'TMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" >> "$f"; done
true
remediation.guidance: Review /etc/bashrc, /etc/profile, and all files ending in *.sh in the /etc/profile.d/ directory and remove or edit all TMOUT=_n_ entries to follow local site policy. TMOUT should not exceed 900 or be equal to 0. Configure TMOUT in one of the following files: • A file in the /etc/profile.d/ directory ending in .sh • /etc/profile • /etc/bashrc Example command to set TMOUT to 900 seconds in a file in /etc/profile.d/: # printf '%s\n' "# Set TMOUT to 900 seconds" "typeset -xr TMOUT=900" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmout.sh TMOUT configuration examples: typeset -xr TMOUT=900 Deprecated methods: • As multiple lines: TMOUT=900 readonly TMOUT export TMOUT • As a single line: readonly TMOUT=900 ; export TMOUT

If not specified, the system-provided default is used. The value given must always be a 4-digit octal number, with the initial digit being zero. The legacy $umask parameter sets the rsyslogd process' umask. If not specified, the system-provided default is used. The value given must always be a 4-digit octal number, with the initial digit being zero. The legacy $FileCreateMode parameter allows the setting of the mode with

description: Log files contain information from many services on the the local system, or in the event of a centralized log server, others systems logs as well. In general log files are found in /var/log/, although application can be configured to store logs elsewhere. Should your application store logs in another, ensure to run the same test on that location.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

      [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=(" - File: \"$l_fname\" is:" "${a_out2[@]}")
   }
   while IFS= read -r -d $'"'"'\0'"'"' l_file; do
      while IFS=: read -r l_fname l_mode l_user l_group; do

                  perm_mask='"'"'0137'"'"' l_auser="(root|syslog)" l_agroup="(root|adm)"

      printf '"'"'\n%s'"'"' "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""

title: Ensure local interactive user home directories are configured
description: The user home directory is space defined for the particular user to set local environment variables and to store personal files. While the system administrator can establish secure permissions for users' home directories, the users can easily override these. Users can be defined in /etc/passwd without a home directory or with a home directory that does not actually exist.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{

   [ "$l_users" -gt 10000 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "  ** INFO **" \
   "  $l_users Local interactive users found on the system" "  This may be a long running check" "  **********"
   while IFS=" " read -r l_user l_home; do

         a_exists2+=("  - User: \"$l_user\" Home Directory: \"$l_home\" Doesn'"'"'t exist")
      fi
   done <<< "$(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '"'"'$(NF) ~ pat { print $1 " " $(NF-1) }'"'"' /etc/passwd)"
   [ "${#a_exists2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_exists2[@]}") || \
   a_output+=("  - All interactive users home directories exist")
   [ "${#a_mode2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_mode2[@]}") || \
   a_output+=("  - All interactive users home directories are mode \"$l_max\" or more restrictive")
   [ "${#a_owner2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_owner2[@]}") || \
   a_output+=("  - All interactive users own their home directory")
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then

   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

description: 5/28/2026 2.0.0 UPDATED RECOMMENDATION: 6.2.3.1 - Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected - Sections Modified: Audit Procedure 5/28/2026 2.0.0 UPDATED RECOMMENDATION: 6.2.3.2 - Ensure actions as another user are always logged - Sections Modified: Remediation Procedure; Audit Procedure Date Version Changes for this version 5/28/2026 2.0.0 UPDATED RECOMMENDATION: 6.2.3.3 - Ensure events that modify the sudo log file are collected - Sections Modified: Remediation Procedure; Audit Procedure 5/28/2026 2.0.0 UPDATED RECOMMENDATION: 6.2.3.4 - Ensure events that modify dat

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output2=(); a_output3=()
   l_maxsize="1000" # Maximum number of local interactive users before warning (Default 1,000)
   l_valid_shells="^($( awk -F\/ '"'"'$NF != "nologin" {print}'"'"' /etc/shells | sed -rn '"'"'/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}'"'"' | paste -s -d '"'"'|'"'"' - ))$"
   a_user_and_home=() # Create array with local users and their home directories
   while read -r l_local_user l_local_user_home; do # Populate array with users and user home location
      [[ -n "$l_local_user" && -n "$l_local_user_home" ]] && a_user_and_home+=("$l_local_user:$l_local_user_home")
   done <<< "$(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '"'"'$(NF) ~ pat { print $1 " " $(NF-1) }'"'"' /etc/passwd)"
   l_asize="${#a_user_and_home[@]}" # Here if we want to look at number of users before proceeding
   [ "${#a_user_and_home[@]}" -gt "$l_maxsize" ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "  ** INFO **" \
   "  - \"$l_asize\" Local interactive users found on the system" \
   "  - This may be a long running check" ""
   file_access_chk()
   {
      a_access_out=()
      l_max="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_mask)) )"
      if [ $(( $l_mode & $l_mask )) -gt 0 ]; then
         a_access_out+=("  - File: \"$l_hdfile\" is mode: \"$l_mode\" and should be mode: \"$l_max\" or more restrictive")
      fi
      if [[ ! "$l_owner" =~ ($l_user) ]]; then
         a_access_out+=("  - File: \"$l_hdfile\" owned by: \"$l_owner\" and should be owned by \"${l_user//|/ or }\"")
      fi
      if [[ ! "$l_gowner" =~ ($l_group) ]]; then
         a_access_out+=("  - File: \"$l_hdfile\" group owned by: \"$l_gowner\" and should be group owned by \"${l_group//|/ or }\"")
      fi
   }
   while IFS=: read -r l_user l_home; do
      a_dot_file=(); a_netrc=(); a_netrc_warn=(); a_bhout=(); a_hdirout=()
      if [ -d "$l_home" ]; then
         l_group="$(id -gn "$l_user" | xargs)";l_group="${l_group// /|}"
         while IFS= read -r -d $'"'"'\0'"'"' l_hdfile; do
            while read -r l_mode l_owner l_gowner; do
               case "$(basename "$l_hdfile")" in
                  .forward | .rhost )
                     a_dot_file+=("  - File: \"$l_hdfile\" exists") ;;
                  .netrc )
                     l_mask='"'"'0177'"'"'; file_access_chk
                     if [ "${#a_access_out[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
                        a_netrc+=("${a_access_out[@]}")
                     else
                        a_netrc_warn+=("   - File: \"$l_hdfile\" exists")
                     fi ;;
                  .bash_history )
                     l_mask='"'"'0177'"'"'; file_access_chk

                     [ "${#a_access_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_bhout+=("${a_access_out[@]}") ;;
                  * )
                     l_mask='"'"'0133'"'"'; file_access_chk
                     [ "${#a_access_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_hdirout+=("${a_access_out[@]}") ;;

      fi
      [ "${#a_netrc_warn[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output3+=(" - User: \"$l_user\" Home Directory: \"$l_home\"" "${a_netrc_warn[@]}")
   done <<< "$(printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "${a_user_and_home[@]}")"
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then # If l_output2 is empty, we pass
      [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "  ** WARNING **" "${a_output3[@]}"
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - * Reasons for audit failure * :" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "  ** WARNING **" "${a_output3[@]}"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure access to gpg key files are configured
description: GPG key files are cryptographic keys used by APT to verify the authenticity and integrity of software packages. Each key ensures that packages come from a trusted source and have not been tampered with. These keys are typically stored in keyring directories /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d or /usr/share/keyrings and referenced in repository configuration files using the signed-by option for secure package verification.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1.3

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash
{
   while IFS= read -r l_keypath; do
      l_keyfile="$(readlink -e "$l_keypath" 2>/dev/null)"
      [ -z "$l_keyfile" ] && continue
      case "$l_keyfile" in
        /usr/share/keyrings/*|/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/*) continue ;;
      esac
      stat -Lc '"'"'File: %n Mode: (%#a) User: (%U) Group: (%G)'"'"' "$l_keyfile" | \
      grep -Pv -- '"'"'Mode: \(0?6[04][04]\) User: \(root\) Group: \(root\)'"'"'
   done < <(grep -PRho -- '"'"'\bSigned-By\b\s*[=:]\s*\K\S+'"'"' \
      /etc/apt/sources.list \
      /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.list \
      /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.sources 2>/dev/null | sort -u)
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: Run the following commands to update the access to any file(s) returned in the audit steps above: # chown root:root "/absolute/path/to/file" # chmod u-x,go-wx "/absolute/path/to/file" Example # chown root:root /usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-trixie-security- automatic.gpg # chmod u-x,go-wx /usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-trixie-security- automatic.gpg Note: APT first checks keys specified with the signed-by option in a repository's .sources or .list files. If no key is specified there, it falls back to administrator- managed keyrings in /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d, then system-wide keyrings in /usr/share/keyrings.

title: Ensure access to /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d directory is configured
description: The /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d directory stores individual GPG key files that APT uses to verify the authenticity of packages and repositories.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1.4

audit.command: alt0() { s=$(stat -Lc '%a %u %g' /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d 2>&1) || { echo "step1: $s"; return 1; }; set -- $s; m=$((8#$1)); [ $((m & ~0755)) -eq 0 ] && [ "$2" = 0 ] && [ "$3" = 0 ] || { echo "step1: /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d is mode $1 uid $2 gid $3, want 755 or stricter, uid 0, gid 0"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure repositories are set to https in /etc/apt/sources.list
description: APT supports both HTTP and HTTPS transport for repository access. While official repositories for the target distributions use HTTPS by default, custom or third-party repositories added by administrators may be configured with HTTP. Repositories served over plain HTTP are susceptible to network interception — an attacker positioned between the system and a mirror could suppress specific security updates, withholding patches to keep the system vulnerable to known exploits, or intercept repository metadata to profile installed software versions.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1.10

remediation.command: Edit /etc/apt/sources.list and replace http:// with https:// for each repository URI. Example — legacy .list format: deb https://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm main

title: Ensure AllowInsecureRepositories is configured
description: The APT configuration option Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories controls whether APT is permitted to access repositories that do not have a valid cryptographic signature on their InRelease or Release.gpg metadata files. When set to 1, APT bypasses repository authentication and will download package lists and packages from unsigned or improperly signed repositories without warning. This option should be explicitly set to 0 to enforce repository signature verification.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1.12

audit.command: alt0() { command -v apt-config >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: apt-config not installed"; return 1; }; command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'apt-config dump | grep AllowInsecureRepositories' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories "0";' || { echo step1: missing 'Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories "0";'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Create a configuration file to explicitly disable insecure repository access: # printf '%s\n' "" 'Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories "0";' >> /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99-no-insecure-repositories Verify the setting has taken effect: # apt-config dump | grep AllowInsecureRepositories Note: All configuration files under /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/ are processed in lexicographic order. Where conflicting settings exist, the last one takes precedence. The 99- prefix ensures this setting overrides any earlier configuration.

title: Ensure AllowWeakRepositories is configured
description: The APT configuration option Acquire::AllowWeakRepositories controls whether APT accepts repositories signed with cryptographically weak algorithms. Weak signatures include those using MD5 or SHA-1 hashing algorithms, which are no longer considered cryptographically secure. When set to 1, APT treats repositories signed with these deprecated algorithms as trusted. This option should be explicitly set to 0 to enforce strong signature requirements.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1.13

title: Ensure Acquire::Check-Date is configured
description: The APT configuration option Acquire::Check-Date controls whether APT verifies that the system clock is plausible relative to the Valid-Until field in a repository's Release file. This option should be explicitly set to true to ensure this validation is always active and cannot be silently disabled by other configuration.

title: Ensure update-notifier-motd.service is not in use
description: update-notifier-motd.service is a oneshot systemd unit shipped on Ubuntu by the update-notifier-common package. It executes /usr/lib/update- notifier/update-motd-updates-available, which refreshes the dynamic MOTD fragments in /var/lib/update-notifier/ (most visibly updates-available, the "N packages can be updated, M are security updates" lines surfaced by pam_motd). The same script also drives the motd-news integration via /etc/update-motd.d/50- motd-news, which contacts Ubuntu's motd.ubuntu.com endpoint when ENABLED=1 in /etc/default/motd-news. Note: • update-notifier-motd.service is not pr
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.11

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: systemctl not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'systemctl is-enabled update-notifier-motd.service 2>/dev/null | grep '"'"'enabled'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: systemctl not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'systemctl is-active update-notifier-motd.service 2>/dev/null | grep '"'"'^active'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step2: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: - IF - update-notifier-motd.service is installed (Ubuntu), run the following commands to stop and mask the unit: # systemctl stop update-notifier-motd.service # systemctl mask update-notifier-motd.service Note: • mask is preferred over disable because disable only removes enablement symlinks; a transient activation (e.g., via the companion timer, or systemctl start) will still run the unit. mask redirects the unit to /dev/null so it cannot be started. • This recommendation does not require removing the update-notifier-common package. If the package is also undesired, it may be removed with apt purge update-notifier-common, but that is out of scope for this rule.
