title: Ensure GDM disable-user-list is configured
description: GNOME Display Manager (GDM) handles graphical login for GNOME based systems. The disable-user-list option controls if a list of users is displayed on the login screen By using the lockdown mode in dconf, you can prevent users from changing specific settings.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.2

audit.command: alt0() { command -v gsettings >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: gsettings not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'gsettings writable org.gnome.login-screen disable-user-list' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- false || { echo step1: missing false; return 1; }; command -v gsettings >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: gsettings not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'gsettings get org.gnome.login-screen disable-user-list' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- true || { echo step2: missing true; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; return 0; }
tma_ini_set() { # file section key value
  local f=$1 s=$2 k=$3 v=$4
  [ -e "$f" ] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; : > "$f"; }
  tma_bak "$f"
  awk -v s="$s" -v k="$k" -v v="$v" '
    function flush() { if (insec && !done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } }
    /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { flush(); insec = ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*\\[" s "\\][[:space:]]*$"); print; next }
    insec && $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*" k "[[:space:]]*=" { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } ; next }
    { print }
    END { flush(); if (!done) { print "[" s "]"; print k "=" v } }' "$f" > "$f.tma" && cat "$f.tma" > "$f"; rm -f "$f.tma"
}
tma_grub_regen() {
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ -f /boot/grub2/grub.cfg ]; then grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg
    else for c in /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c"; done; fi
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -f /boot/grub/grub.cfg ] && grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
  fi; return 0
}
tma_cmdline_rm() { # names of kernel args (name or name=value) to drop from the grub defaults
  local a f c k n
  for a in "$@"; do
    for f in /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.d/*.cfg; do
      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" "$f" || continue
      tma_bak "$f"
      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"
    done
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args="$a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  if command -v grub2-editenv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    k=$(grub2-editenv - list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^kernelopts=//p')
    if [ -n "$k" ]; then n=$k; for a in "$@"; do n=$(printf '%s' "$n" | sed -E "s/(^| )${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/ /g"); done
      [ "$n" != "$k" ] && grub2-editenv - set "kernelopts=$n"; fi
  fi
  for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/grub/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do
    [ -f "$c" ] || continue
    for a in "$@"; do sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*(linux|kernelopts)/ s/(^|[ =])${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/\1\3/g" "$c"; done
  done
  return 0
}
tma_cmdline_set() { # name=value pairs forced into GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
  local f=/etc/default/grub kv; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $f"; return 0; }
  for kv in "$@"; do
    tma_cmdline_rm "${kv%%=*}" "${kv%%=*}=[^ \"']*" 2>/dev/null
    tma_bak "$f"
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$f"; then
      sed -i -E "s/^([[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=[\"'])(.*)([\"'])\$/\1\2 ${kv}\3/; s/=([\"']) /=\1/" "$f"
    else printf 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="%s"\n' "$kv" >> "$f"; fi
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --args="$kv" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  return 0
}
prof=local
mkdir -p /etc/dconf/profile /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks
pf() { [ -f "$1" ] || : > "$1"; while IFS= read -r l; do grep -qxF "$l" "$1" || printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$1"; done; }
printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user
system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/$prof
printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user' 'system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/user
cat > /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/00-login-screen <<'TMAEOF'
[org/gnome/login-screen]
disable-user-list=true
TMAEOF
printf '%s\n' /org/gnome/login-screen/disable-user-list > /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks/00-login-screen
command -v dconf >/dev/null 2>&1 && dconf update
true

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; return 0; }
tma_ini_set() { # file section key value
  local f=$1 s=$2 k=$3 v=$4
  [ -e "$f" ] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; : > "$f"; }
  tma_bak "$f"
  awk -v s="$s" -v k="$k" -v v="$v" '
    function flush() { if (insec && !done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } }
    /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { flush(); insec = ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*\\[" s "\\][[:space:]]*$"); print; next }
    insec && $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*" k "[[:space:]]*=" { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done=1 } ; next }
    { print }
    END { flush(); if (!done) { print "[" s "]"; print k "=" v } }' "$f" > "$f.tma" && cat "$f.tma" > "$f"; rm -f "$f.tma"
}
tma_grub_regen() {
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ -f /boot/grub2/grub.cfg ]; then grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg
    else for c in /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c"; done; fi
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -f /boot/grub/grub.cfg ] && grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
  fi; return 0
}
tma_cmdline_rm() { # names of kernel args (name or name=value) to drop from the grub defaults
  local a f c k n
  for a in "$@"; do
    for f in /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.d/*.cfg; do
      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" "$f" || continue
      tma_bak "$f"
      sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX/{ :a; s/([\"' ])${a}(=[^\"' ]*)?([ \"'])/\1\3/; ta; s/  +/ /g; s/ ([\"'])\$/\1/ }" "$f"
    done
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --remove-args="$a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  if command -v grub2-editenv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    k=$(grub2-editenv - list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^kernelopts=//p')
    if [ -n "$k" ]; then n=$k; for a in "$@"; do n=$(printf '%s' "$n" | sed -E "s/(^| )${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/ /g"); done
      [ "$n" != "$k" ] && grub2-editenv - set "kernelopts=$n"; fi
  fi
  for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/grub/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do
    [ -f "$c" ] || continue
    for a in "$@"; do sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*(linux|kernelopts)/ s/(^|[ =])${a}(=[^ ]*)?( |\$)/\1\3/g" "$c"; done
  done
  return 0
}
tma_cmdline_set() { # name=value pairs forced into GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
  local f=/etc/default/grub kv; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $f"; return 0; }
  for kv in "$@"; do
    tma_cmdline_rm "${kv%%=*}" "${kv%%=*}=[^ \"']*" 2>/dev/null
    tma_bak "$f"
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$f"; then
      sed -i -E "s/^([[:space:]]*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=[\"'])(.*)([\"'])\$/\1\2 ${kv}\3/; s/=([\"']) /=\1/" "$f"
    else printf 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="%s"\n' "$kv" >> "$f"; fi
    command -v grubby >/dev/null 2>&1 && grubby --update-kernel ALL --args="$kv" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  return 0
}

mkdir -p /etc/dconf/profile /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks
pf() { [ -f "$1" ] || : > "$1"; while IFS= read -r l; do grep -qxF "$l" "$1" || printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$1"; done; }
printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user
system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/$prof
printf '%s\n' 'user-db:user' 'system-db:local' | pf /etc/dconf/profile/user
cat > /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/00-media-autorun <<'TMAEOF'
[org/gnome/desktop/media-handling]
autorun-never=true
TMAEOF
printf '%s\n' /org/gnome/desktop/media-handling/autorun-never > /etc/dconf/db/$prof.d/locks/00-media-autorun
command -v dconf >/dev/null 2>&1 && dconf update
true

description: Mail Transfer Agents (MTA), such as sendmail and Postfix, are used to listen for incoming mail and transfer the messages to the appropriate user or mail server. If the system is not intended to be a mail server, it is recommended that the MTA be configured to only process local mail.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=(); a_port_list=("25" "465" "587")
   for l_port_number in "${a_port_list[@]}"; do
      if ss -plntu | grep -P -- '"'"':'"'"'"$l_port_number"'"'"'\h'"'"' | grep -Pvq -- '"'"'\h+(127\.0\.0\.1|\[?::1\]?):'"'"'"$l_port_number"'"'"'\b'"'"'; then
         a_output2+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is listening on a non- loopback network interface")
      else
         a_output+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is not listening on a non- loopback network interface")
      fi
   done
   if command -v postconf &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(postconf -n inet_interfaces)"
   elif command -v exim &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(exim -bP local_interfaces)"
   elif command -v sendmail &> /dev/null; then
      l_interfaces="$(grep -i "O DaemonPortOptions=" /etc/mail/sendmail.cf | grep -oP '"'"'(?<=Addr=)[^,+]+'"'"' | grep -v '"'"'^127\.0\.0\.1$'"'"')"
   fi
   if [ -n "$l_interfaces" ]; then
      if grep -Pqi '"'"'\ball\b'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to all network interfaces")
      elif ! grep -Pqi '"'"'(inet_interfaces\h*=\h*)?(0\.0\.0\.0|::1|loopback- only)'"'"' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then
         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to a network interface" " \"$l_interfaces\"")
      else
         a_output+=(" - MTA is not bound to a non loopback network interface" "   \"$l_interfaces\"")
      fi
   else
      a_output+=(" - MTA not detected or in use")
   fi
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"
   else
      printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure all users last password change date is in the past
description: All users should have a password change date in the past.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.1.6

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
 while IFS= read -r l_user; do
 l_change_raw=$(chage --list "$l_user" | grep '"'"'^Last password change'"'"' | cut - d: -f2 | tr -d '"'"' '"'"')
 [ "$l_change_raw" = "never" ] && continue
 l_change=$(date -u -d "$l_change_raw" +%s 2>/dev/null) || continue
 if [[ "$l_change" -gt "$(date +%s)" ]]; then
 echo "User: \"$l_user\" last password change was \"$l_change_raw\""
 fi

}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Investigate any users with a password change date in the future and correct them. Locking the account, expiring the password, or resetting the password manually may be appropriate. Examples Reset last change date to today for a single user: # chage -d "$(date +%Y-%m-%d)" <user> Force password change on next login (recommended companion): # chage -d 0 <user>

title: Ensure root path integrity
description: The root user can execute any command on the system and could be fooled into executing programs unintentionally if the PATH is not set correctly.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.2.5

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
 a_output2=() l_pmask="0022"
 l_maxperm="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"
 l_root_path="$(sudo su - root -c env | awk -F= '"'"'$1=="PATH"{print $2}'"'"')"
 IFS=":" read -ra a_path_loc <<< "$l_root_path"
 grep -q -- "::" <<< "$l_root_path" && \
 a_output2+=(" - root'"'"'s path contains a empty directory (::)")
 grep -Pq -- ":\h*$" <<< "$l_root_path" && \
 a_output2+=(" - root'"'"'s path contains a trailing (:)")
 grep -Pq -- '"'"'(^\h*|:)\.(:|\h*$)'"'"' <<< "$l_root_path" && \
 a_output2+=(" - root'"'"'s path contains current working directory (.)")
 for l_path in "${a_path_loc[@]}"; do
 if [ -d "$l_path" ]; then
 while IFS=: read -r l_fmode l_fown; do
 [ "$l_fown" != "root" ] && \
 a_output2+=(" - Directory: \"$l_path\" is owned by: \"$l_fown\"" \
 " should be owned by \"root\"")
 [ $(( $l_fmode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ] && \
 a_output2+=(" - Directory: \"$l_path\" is mode: \"$l_fmode\"" \
 " and should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive")
 done <<< "$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a:%U'"'"' "$l_path")"
 else
 a_output2+=(" - \"$l_path\" is not a directory")
 fi
 done
 if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
 printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "Non-compliant path elements:" "${a_output2[@]}"
 fi
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Correct or justify any: • Locations that are not directories • Empty directories (::) • Trailing (:) • Current working directory (.) • Non root owned directories • Directories that less restrictive than mode 0755

title: Ensure root user umask is configured
description: The user file-creation mode mask (umask) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (rwxrwxrwx), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (rw-rw- rw-). The umask modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The umask is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the umask are cleared in the resulting file mode. umask can be set with either Octal or Symbolic values: • Octal (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.2.6

audit.command: alt0() { o=$(bash -c 'grep -Psi -- '"'"'^\h*umask\h+((\d{1,2}(\d[^7]|[^2- 7]\d)\b)|(u=[rwx]{1,3},)?(((g=[rx]?[rx]?w[rx]?[rx]?\b)(,o=[rwx]{1,3})?)|((g=[ wrx]{1,3},)?o=[wrx]{1,3}\b)))'"'"' /root/.profile /root/.bashrc' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit /root/.profile and /root/.bashrc and either: • remove, comment out, or update any line with umask. - OR - • update any line that includes umask to a value of 0027 or more restrictive. Example: umask 027 Note: the Recommendation "Ensure default user umask is configured" includes guidance to set the default umask

title: Ensure accounts without a valid login shell are locked

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_valid_shells="^($(awk -F\/ '"'"'$NF != "nologin" {print}'"'"' /etc/shells | sed -rn '"'"'/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}'"'"' | paste -s -d '"'"'|'"'"' - ))$"
   while IFS= read -r l_user; do
      passwd -S "$l_user" | awk '"'"'$2 !~ /^L/ {print "Account: \"" $1 "\" does not have a valid login shell and is not locked"}'"'"'
   done < <(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '"'"'($1 != "root" && $(NF) !~ pat) {print $1}'"'"' /etc/passwd)
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured
description: TMOUT is an environmental setting that determines the timeout of a shell in seconds. • TMOUT=n - Sets the shell timeout to n seconds. A setting of TMOUT=0 disables timeout. • readonly TMOUT- Sets the TMOUT environmental variable as readonly, preventing unwanted modification during run-time. • export TMOUT - exports the TMOUT variable System Wide Shell Configuration Files: • /etc/profile - used to set system wide environmental variables on users shells. The variables are sometimes the same ones that are in the .bash_profile, however this file is used to set an initial PATH or PS1 for all shell
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.3.2

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
 a_output=(); a_output2=(); l_tmout_set="900"
 f_tmout_read_chk()
 {
 a_out=(); a_out2=()
 l_tmout_readonly="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\- xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\breadonly\h+TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
 l_tmout_export="$(grep -P -- '"'"'^\h*(typeset\h\- xr\hTMOUT=\d+|([^#\n\r]+)?\bexport\b([^#\n\r]+\b)?TMOUT\b)'"'"' "$l_file")"
 if [ -n "$l_tmout_readonly" ]; then
 a_out+=(" - Readonly is set as: \"$l_tmout_readonly\" in: \"$l_file\"")
 else
 a_out2+=(" - Readonly is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
 fi
 if [ -n "$l_tmout_export" ]; then
 a_out+=(" - Export is set as: \"$l_tmout_export\" in: \"$l_file\"")
 else
 a_out2+=(" - Export is not set in: \"$l_file\"")
 fi
 }
 while IFS= read -r l_file; do
 l_tmout_value="$(grep -Po -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT=\d+\b'"'"' "$l_file" | awk - F= '"'"'{print $2}'"'"')"
 f_tmout_read_chk
 if [ -n "$l_tmout_value" ]; then
 if [[ "$l_tmout_value" -le "$l_tmout_set" && "$l_tmout_value" -gt "0" ]]; then
 a_output+=(" - TMOUT is set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")
 [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output+=("${a_out[@]}")
 [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out[@]}")
 fi
 if [[ "$l_tmout_value" -gt "$l_tmout_set" || "$l_tmout_value" -le "0" ]]; then
 a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is incorrectly set to: \"$l_tmout_value\" in: \"$l_file\"")
 [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=(" ** Incorrect TMOUT value **" "${a_out[@]}")
 [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=("${a_out2[@]}")
 fi
 else
 [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not set" "${a_out[@]}")
 [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not set" "${a_out2[@]}")
 fi
 done < <(grep -Pls -- '"'"'^([^#\n\r]+)?\bTMOUT\b'"'"' /etc/*bashrc /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/*.sh)
 [[ "${#a_output[@]}" -le 0 && "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]] && a_output2+=(" - TMOUT is not configured")
 if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
 printf '"'"'%s\n'"'"' "Non-compliant TMOUT configuration:" "${a_output2[@]}"
 fi
}' 2>&1); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_ts=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$tma_ts"; }
tma_applied() { return 0; }

# make every umask line in the given files at least 027
tma_umask_fix() { for f in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  grep -Eqi '^[[:space:]]*umask[[:space:]]' "$f" || continue
  t=$(mktemp); ch=0
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    if [[ $line =~ ^([[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+)0*([0-7]{1,4})([[:space:]#].*)?$ ]]; then
      v=$((8#${BASH_REMATCH[2]})); n=$((v | 8#027))
      if [ "$n" != "$v" ]; then line="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}$(printf '%03o' $n)${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"; ch=1; fi
    elif [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+[ugoa]*= ]] && [[ $line =~ (g=[rwx]*w|o=[rwx]*[rwx]) ]]; then
      line="umask 027"; ch=1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$t"
  done < "$f"
  if [ $ch = 1 ]; then tma_bak "$f"; cat "$t" > "$f"; fi
  rm -f "$t"
done; }
N=900
# one authoritative file; any other TMOUT assignment is commented out (audit demands readonly+export in each file mentioning it)
for f in /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile.d/*.sh; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  [ "$f" = /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh ] && continue
  grep -Eq '^[^#]*\bTMOUT\b' "$f" || continue
  tma_bak "$f"; sed -i -E '/^[[:space:]]*#/! s/^([^#]*\bTMOUT\b.*)$/# tmaegis: \1/' "$f"
done
mkdir -p /etc/profile.d
printf '# CIS: idle shell timeout\nTMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
for f in /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile; do [ -f "$f" ] && ! grep -q '^TMOUT=' "$f" && [ "$f" = /etc/bash/bashrc ] && printf 'TMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" >> "$f"; done
true
remediation.guidance: Review /etc/bashrc, /etc/profile, and all files ending in *.sh in the /etc/profile.d/ directory and remove or edit all TMOUT=_n_ entries to follow local site policy. TMOUT should not exceed 900 or be equal to 0. Configure TMOUT in one of the following files: • A file in the /etc/profile.d/ directory ending in .sh • /etc/profile • /etc/bashrc Example command to set TMOUT to 900 seconds in a file in /etc/profile.d/: # printf '%s\n' "# Set TMOUT to 900 seconds" "typeset -xr TMOUT=900" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmout.sh TMOUT configuration examples: typeset -xr TMOUT=900 Deprecated methods: • As multiple lines: TMOUT=900 readonly TMOUT export TMOUT • As a single line: readonly TMOUT=900 ; export TMOUT

audit.command: alt0() { command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: rpm not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'rpm -q openldap-clients' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'package openldap-clients is not installed' || { echo step1: missing 'package openldap-clients is not installed'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to remove the openldap-clients package: # dnf remove openldap-clients

title: Ensure nologin is not listed in /etc/shells
description: /etc/shells is a text file which contains the full pathnames of valid login shells. This file is consulted by chsh and available to be queried by other programs. Be aware that there are programs which consult this file to find out if a user is a normal user; for example, FTP daemons traditionally disallow access to users with shells not included in this file.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Ps '"'"'^\h*([^#\n\r]+)?\/nologin\b'"'"' /etc/shells' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit /etc/shells and remove any lines that include nologin

title: Ensure auditd service is enabled and active
description: Turn on the auditd daemon to record system events.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: systemctl not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'systemctl is-enabled auditd | grep '"'"'^enabled'"'"'' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- enabled || { echo step1: missing enabled; return 1; }; command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: systemctl not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'systemctl is-active auditd | grep '"'"'^active'"'"'' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- active || { echo step2: missing active; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to unmask, enable and start auditd: # systemctl unmask auditd # systemctl enable auditd # systemctl start auditd

title: Ensure audit logs are not automatically deleted
description: The max_log_file_action setting determines how to handle the audit log file reaching the max file size. A value of keep_logs will rotate the logs but never delete old logs.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep max_log_file_action /etc/audit/auditd.conf' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'max_log_file_action = keep_logs' || { echo step1: missing 'max_log_file_action = keep_logs'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Set the following parameter in /etc/audit/auditd.conf: max_log_file_action = keep_logs

title: Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected
description: Monitor scope changes for system administrators. The file /etc/sudoers, or files in /etc/sudoers.d, will be written to when the file(s) or related attributes have changed. The audit records will be tagged with the identifier "scope".

alt0() { o=$(bash -c 'awk '"'"'/^ *-w/ &&//etc/sudoers/ &&/ +-p *wa/ &&(/ key= *[!-~]* *$/||/ -k *[!-~]* *$/)'"'"' /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules' 2>&1); printf '%s
' "$o" | tr -s ' 	' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- '-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope' || { echo step1: missing '-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope'; return 1; }; printf '%s
' "$o" | tr -s ' 	' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- '-w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope' || { echo step1: missing '-w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope'; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'auditctl -l | awk '"'"'/^ *-w/ &&//etc/sudoers/ &&/ +-p *wa/ &&(/ key= *[!-~]* *$/||/ -k *[!-~]* *$/)'"'"'' 2>&1); printf '%s
' "$o" | tr -s ' 	' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- '-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope' || { echo step2: missing '-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope'; return 1; }; printf '%s

While not recommended for production systems, permissive mode can be helpful for SELinux policy development. • Disabled - Is strongly discouraged; n

description: fs.protected_symlinks controls how the kernel handles symbolic links. audit.command: m=overlay; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/overlay*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep max_log_file_action /etc/audit/auditd.conf' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'max_log_file_action = keep_logs' || { echo step1: missing 'max_log_file_action = keep_logs'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Set the following parameter in /etc/audit/auditd.conf: max_log_file_action = keep_logs

title: Ensure the audit log file directory mode is configured
description: The audit log directory contains audit log files.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_perm_mask="0027"
   if [ -e "/etc/audit/auditd.conf" ]; then
      l_audit_log_directory="$(dirname "$(awk -F= '"'"'/^\s*log_file\s*/{print $2}'"'"' /etc/audit/auditd.conf | xargs)")"
      if [ -d "$l_audit_log_directory" ]; then
         l_maxperm="$(printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_perm_mask )) )"
         l_directory_mode="$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a'"'"' "$l_audit_log_directory")"
         if [ $(( $l_directory_mode & $l_perm_mask )) -gt 0 ]; then
            echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n  - Directory: \"$l_audit_log_directory\" is mode: \"$l_directory_mode\"\n     (should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive)\n"
         else
            echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** PASS **\n  - Directory: \"$l_audit_log_directory\" is mode: \"$l_directory_mode\"\n     (should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive)\n"
         fi
      else
         echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n  - Log file directory not set in \"/etc/audit/auditd.conf\" please set log file directory"
      fi
   else
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n  - File: \"/etc/audit/auditd.conf\" not found\n  - ** Verify auditd is installed **"

tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do

  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }

tma_nl() { [ -s "$1" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c1 "$1")" ] && echo >> "$1"; return 0; }
tma_kv() { # file key value : 'key = value' style (auditd.conf); replaces every uncommented line

title: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is sufficient
description: In the kernel-level audit subsystem, a socket buffer queue is used to hold audit events. Whenever a new audit event is received, it is logged and prepared to be added to this queue. The kernel boot parameter audit_backlog_limit=N, with N representing the amount of messages, will ensure that a queue cannot grow beyond a certain size. If an audit event is logged which would grow the queue beyond this limit, then a failure occurs and is handled according to the system configuration

remediation.guidance: Edit /etc/default/grub and add audit_backlog_limit=N to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX. The recommended size for N is 8192 or larger. Example: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit_backlog_limit=8192" Run the following command to update the grub2 configuration: # update-grub

title: Ensure Xwayland is configured
description: Xwayland is a compatibility layer that allows legacy X11 applications to run within a Wayland environment. It's effectively an X server that runs as a Wayland client, enabling existing X11 software to be displayed on a Wayland compositor.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v sed >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: sed not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'sed -n '"'"'/\[daemon\]/,/\[/p'"'"' /etc/gdm/custom.conf | grep -Psi '"'"'^\h*waylandenable\b'"'"'' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- WaylandEnable=false || { echo step1: missing WaylandEnable=false; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit the file /etc/gdm/custom.conf and uncomment or add the following line in the [daemon] block: WaylandEnable=false Example: # GDM configuration storage [daemon] WaylandEnable=false [security] [xdmcp] [chooser] [debug] # Uncomment the line below to turn on debugging #Enable=true

title: Ensure nologin is not listed in /etc/shells
description: /etc/shells is a text file which contains the full pathnames of valid login shells. This file is consulted by chsh and available to be queried by other programs. Be aware that there are programs which consult this file to find out if a user is a normal user; for example, FTP daemons traditionally disallow access to users with shells not included in this file.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Ps '"'"'^\h*([^#\n\r]+)?\/nologin\b'"'"' /etc/shells' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit /etc/shells and remove any lines that include nologin

title: Ensure rsyslog-gnutls is installed
description: TLS protocol support for rsyslog (GnuTLS). This netstream plugin allows rsyslog to send and receive encrypted syslog messages via the syslog-transport-tls IETF standard protocol using GnuTLS.

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to install rsyslog-gnutls: # apt install rsyslog-gnutls

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to unmask, enable and start auditd: # systemctl unmask auditd # systemctl enable auditd # systemctl start auditd

title: Ensure auditing for processes that start prior to auditd is enabled
description: Configure grub2 so that processes that are capable of being audited can be audited even if they start up prior to auditd startup.

audit.command: alt0() { command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: find not installed"; return 1; }; command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'find /boot -type f -name '"'"'grub.cfg'"'"' -exec grep -Ph -- '"'"'^\h*linux'"'"' {} + | grep -v '"'"'audit=1'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit /etc/default/grub or a file in /etc/default/grub.d/ ending in .cfg adding audit=1 to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX: Example: printf "\n%s\n" 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit=1"' >> /etc/default/grub.d/40- custom.cfg Run the following command to update the grub2 configuration: # update-grub

title: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is configured
description: In the kernel-level audit subsystem, a socket buffer queue is used to hold audit events. Whenever a new audit event is received, it is logged and prepared to be added to this queue. The kernel boot parameter audit_backlog_limit=N, with N representing the amount of messages, will ensure that a queue cannot grow beyond a certain size. If an audit event is logged which would grow the queue beyond this limit, then a failure occurs and is handled according to the system configuration

audit.command: alt0() { command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: find not installed"; return 1; }; command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'find /boot -type f -name '"'"'grub.cfg'"'"' -exec grep -Ph -- '"'"'^\h*linux'"'"' {} + | grep -Pv '"'"'audit_backlog_limit=\d+\b'"'"'' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit /etc/default/grub or a file in /etc/default/grub.d/ ending in .cfg adding audit_backlog_limit=N to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX. The recommended size for N is 8192 or larger`: Example: # printf "\n%s\n" 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit_backlog_limit=8192"' >> /etc/default/grub.d/40-custom.cfg Run the following command to update the grub2 configuration: # update-grub

title: Ensure audit logs are not automatically deleted
description: The max_log_file_action setting determines how to handle the audit log file reaching the max file size. A value of keep_logs will rotate the logs but never delete old logs.

remediation.guidance: Set the following parameter in /etc/audit/auditd.conf: max_log_file_action = keep_logs

title: Ensure the audit configuration is immutable
description: Set system audit so that audit rules cannot be modified with auditctl . Setting the flag -e 2 forces audit to be put in immutable mode. Audit changes can only be made on system reboot. Note: This setting will require the system to be rebooted to update the active auditd configuration settings.

title: Ensure the audit log file directory mode is configured
description: The audit log directory contains audit log files.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_perm_mask="0027"
   if [ -e "/etc/audit/auditd.conf" ]; then
      l_audit_log_directory="$(dirname "$(awk -F= '"'"'/^\s*log_file\s*/{print $2}'"'"' /etc/audit/auditd.conf | xargs)")"
      if [ -d "$l_audit_log_directory" ]; then
         l_maxperm="$(printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_perm_mask )) )"
         l_directory_mode="$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a'"'"' "$l_audit_log_directory")"
         if [ $(( $l_directory_mode & $l_perm_mask )) -gt 0 ]; then
            echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n  - Directory: \"$l_audit_log_directory\" is mode: \"$l_directory_mode\"\n     (should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive)\n"
         else
            echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** PASS **\n  - Directory: \"$l_audit_log_directory\" is mode: \"$l_directory_mode\"\n     (should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive)\n"
         fi
      else
         echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n  - Log file directory not set in \"/etc/audit/auditd.conf\" please set log file directory"
      fi
   else
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n  - File: \"/etc/audit/auditd.conf\" not found\n  - ** Verify auditd is installed **"
   fi
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to configure the audit log directory to have a mode of "0750" or less permissive: # chmod g-w,o-rwx "$(dirname "$(awk -F= '/^\s*log_file\s*/{print $2}' /etc/audit/auditd.conf | xargs)")"

title: Ensure audit log files mode is configured
description: Audit log files contain information about the system and system activity.

alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{

title: Ensure audit log files owner is configured
description: Audit log files contain information about the system and system activity.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_output="" l_output2=""
   if [ -e "/etc/audit/auditd.conf" ]; then

   fi
   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then
      l_output="$l_output\n  - All files in \"$l_audit_log_directory\" are owned by user: \"root\"\n"
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** PASS **\n - * Correctly configured * :$l_output"

audit.command: alt0() { command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: find not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'find /etc/audit/ -type f \( -name '"'"'*.conf'"'"' -o -name '"'"'*.rules'"'"' \) ! -user root' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

title: Ensure audit tools mode is configured
description: Audit tools include, but are not limited to, vendor-provided and open source audit tools needed to successfully view and manipulate audit information system activity and records. Audit tools include custom queries and report generators.

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_output="" l_output2="" l_perm_mask="0022"
   l_maxperm="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_perm_mask )) )"
   a_audit_tools=("/sbin/auditctl" "/sbin/aureport" "/sbin/ausearch" "/sbin/autrace" "/sbin/auditd" "/sbin/augenrules")
   for l_audit_tool in "${a_audit_tools[@]}"; do
      l_mode="$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a'"'"' "$l_audit_tool")"
      if [ $(( "$l_mode" & "$l_perm_mask" )) -gt 0 ]; then
         l_output2="$l_output2\n - Audit tool \"$l_audit_tool\" is mode: \"$l_mode\" and should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive"
      else
         l_output="$l_output\n - Audit tool \"$l_audit_tool\" is correctly configured to mode: \"$l_mode\""
      fi
   done
   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** PASS **\n - * Correctly configured * :$l_output"
   else
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n - * Reasons for audit failure * :$l_output2\n"
      [ -n "$l_output" ] && echo -e "\n - * Correctly configured * :\n$l_output\n"
   fi
   unset a_audit_tools
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to remove more permissive mode from the audit tools: # chmod go-w /sbin/auditctl /sbin/aureport /sbin/ausearch /sbin/autrace /sbin/auditd /sbin/augenrules

tma_nl() { [ -s "$1" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c1 "$1")" ] && echo >> "$1"; return 0; }
tma_kv() { # file key value : 'key = value' style (auditd.conf); replaces every uncommented line

tma_ini_set() { # file section key value : systemd ini 'Key=value'

title: Ensure overlay kernel module is not available
description: The Linux overlay kernel module, commonly referred to as Overlayfs, is a union mount filesystem. It allows the user to overlay one file system on top of another, and creates a single, unified view.

audit.command: m=overlay; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/overlay*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Unload and disable the overlay kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the overlay kernel module: # modprobe -r overlay 2>/dev/null # rmmod overlay 2>/dev/null 2. Perform the following to disable the overlay kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install overlay /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "install overlay /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60- overlay.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist overlay in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "blacklist overlay" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-overlay.conf

title: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is configured

tma_ini_set() { # file section key value : systemd ini 'Key=value'
  f=$1; s=$2; k=$3; v=$4
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; [ -f "$f" ] || : > "$f"; tma_nl "$f"
  sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*$k[[:space:]]*=/d" "$f"
  if grep -q "^\[$s\]" "$f"; then sed -i "/^\[$s\]/a $k=$v" "$f"; else printf '[%s]\n%s=%s\n' "$s" "$k" "$v" >> "$f"; fi; }
tma_clear() { # path octal-mask : remove the mask bits from the file mode
  [ -e "$1" ] || return 0
  m=$(stat -Lc %a "$1")
  [ $((8#$m & 8#$2)) -eq 0 ] || chmod "$(printf '%o' $((8#$m & ~8#$2 & 8#7777)))" "$1"; }
tma_rule() { # rules.d-filename audit-rule-line : append when missing (whitespace-normalised)
  f=/etc/audit/rules.d/$1; shift; l=$*
  mkdir -p /etc/audit/rules.d; [ -f "$f" ] || : > "$f"
  if ! tr -s ' \t' '  ' < "$f" | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- "$l"; then tma_nl "$f"; printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$f"; fi
  chown root:root "$f"; chmod 640 "$f"; }
tma_rules_load() { command -v augenrules >/dev/null 2>&1 && augenrules --load >/dev/null 2>&1; true; }
tma_audit_logdir() {
  d=$(awk -F= '/^[[:space:]]*log_file[[:space:]]*=/{print $2}' /etc/audit/auditd.conf 2>/dev/null | xargs 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$d" ] && dirname "$d" || echo /var/log/audit; }
tma_grub_arg() { # key=value : add/replace in GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX and regenerate grub.cfg
  a=$1; k=${a%%=*}; g=/etc/default/grub
  [ -f "$g" ] || { echo "no $g: bootloader not managed by grub defaults" >&2; return 0; }
  tma_bak "$g"
  if ! grep -q '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$g"; then tma_nl "$g"; printf 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="%s"\n' "$a" >> "$g"
  elif grep -E '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$g" | grep -Eq "[\"' ]$k(=|[\"' ])"; then
    sed -i -E "/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#([\"' ])$k(=[^\"' ]*)?([\"' ])#\1$a\3#" "$g"
  else
    sed -i -E "/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#([\"'])\$#  $a\1#; /^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#=([\"'])  #=\1#; /^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#   *# #g" "$g"
  fi
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg >/dev/null 2>&1; fi
  true; }
command -v aide >/dev/null 2>&1 || tma_pkg_install aide
sbin=$(readlink -f /sbin)
if [ -f /etc/aide.conf ]; then cf=/etc/aide.conf
elif [ -f /etc/aide/aide.conf ]; then cf=/etc/aide/aide.conf
else echo "AIDE configuration file not found" >&2; exit 0; fi

grep -Ev '^[[:space:]]*(/usr)?/sbin/(auditctl|auditd|ausearch|aureport|autrace|augenrules)[[:space:]]|^# Audit Tools$' "$cf" > "$tmp"

{ echo '# Audit Tools'

remediation.guidance: For new installations, during installation create a custom partition setup and specify a separate partition for /tmp. For systems that were previously installed, configure /etc/fstab as appropriate. Example: tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0 Note: This change will no be effected until the system has been re-booted or a re-mount /tmp command is executed. title: Ensure the SELinux mode is enforcing
description: SELinux can run in one of three modes: disabled, permissive, or enforcing: • Enforcing - Is the default, and recommended, mode of operation; in enforcing mode SELinux operates normally, enforcing the loaded security policy on the entire system. • Permissive - The system acts as if SELinux is enforcing the loaded security policy, including labeling objects and emitting access denial entries in the logs, but it does not actually deny any operations. While not recommended for production systems, permissive mode can be helpful for SELinux policy development. • Disabled - Is strongly discouraged; n
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 Benchmark v4.0.0 - 1.3.1.5

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Pi -- '"'"'^\h*SELINUX=enforcing\b'"'"' /etc/selinux/config' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- SELINUX=enforcing || { echo step1: missing SELINUX=enforcing; return 1; }; command -v getenforce >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: getenforce not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c getenforce 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- Enforcing || { echo step2: missing Enforcing; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: 1. Edit /etc/selinux/config and update the SELINUX parameter to SELINUX=enforcing Example: SELINUX=enforcing 2. Update the SELinux running state to enforcing: • If SELinux is currently disabled: Run the following command to create /.autorelabel: # touch /.autorelabel Run the following command to reboot the system: # reboot WARNING: The autorelabel may be a long running process and require significant downtime. This should be planed for before executing the reboot! • If SELinux is not currently disabled: Run the following commands to set SELinux's running mode to Enforcing: # setenforce 1

title: Ensure audit tools mode is configured
description: Audit tools include, but are not limited to, vendor-provided and open source audit tools needed to successfully view and manipulate audit information system activity and records. Audit tools include custom queries and report generators.
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 Benchmark v1.0.1 - 6.3.4.8

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_output="" l_output2="" l_perm_mask="0022"
   l_maxperm="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_perm_mask )) )"
   a_audit_tools=("/sbin/auditctl" "/sbin/aureport" "/sbin/ausearch" "/sbin/autrace" "/sbin/auditd" "/sbin/augenrules")
   for l_audit_tool in "${a_audit_tools[@]}"; do
      l_mode="$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a'"'"' "$l_audit_tool")"
      if [ $(( "$l_mode" & "$l_perm_mask" )) -gt 0 ]; then
         l_output2="$l_output2\n - Audit tool \"$l_audit_tool\" is mode: \"$l_mode\" and should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive"
      else
         l_output="$l_output\n - Audit tool \"$l_audit_tool\" is correctly configured to mode: \"$l_mode\""
      fi
   done
   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** PASS **\n - * Correctly configured * :$l_output"
   else
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n - * Reasons for audit failure * :$l_output2\n"
      [ -n "$l_output" ] && echo -e "\n - * Correctly configured * :\n$l_output\n"
   fi
   unset a_audit_tools
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

audit.command: alt0() { command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: find not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'find /etc/audit/ -type f \( -name '"'"'*.conf'"'"' -o -name '"'"'*.rules'"'"' \) ! -group root' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to change group to root: # find /etc/audit/ -type f \( -name '*.conf' -o -name '*.rules' \) ! -group root -exec chgrp root {} +

title: Ensure audit tools mode is configured
description: Audit tools include, but are not limited to, vendor-provided and open source audit tools needed to successfully view and manipulate audit information system activity and records. Audit tools include custom queries and report generators.
reference: CIS SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 Benchmark v2.0.1 - 6.3.4.8

audit.command:
alt0() { o=$(bash -c '#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_output="" l_output2="" l_perm_mask="0022"
   l_maxperm="$( printf '"'"'%o'"'"' $(( 0777 & ~$l_perm_mask )) )"
   a_audit_tools=("/sbin/auditctl" "/sbin/aureport" "/sbin/ausearch" "/sbin/autrace" "/sbin/auditd" "/sbin/augenrules")
   for l_audit_tool in "${a_audit_tools[@]}"; do
      l_mode="$(stat -Lc '"'"'%#a'"'"' "$l_audit_tool")"
      if [ $(( "$l_mode" & "$l_perm_mask" )) -gt 0 ]; then
         l_output2="$l_output2\n - Audit tool \"$l_audit_tool\" is mode: \"$l_mode\" and should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive"
      else
         l_output="$l_output\n - Audit tool \"$l_audit_tool\" is correctly configured to mode: \"$l_mode\""
      fi
   done
   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** PASS **\n - * Correctly configured * :$l_output"
   else
      echo -e "\n- Audit Result:\n  ** FAIL **\n - * Reasons for audit failure * :$l_output2\n"
      [ -n "$l_output" ] && echo -e "\n - * Correctly configured * :\n$l_output\n"
   fi
   unset a_audit_tools
}' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -q '\*\* PASS \*\*' || { echo "step1: script did not report PASS"; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to remove more permissive mode from the audit tools: # chmod go-w /sbin/auditctl /sbin/aureport /sbin/ausearch /sbin/autrace /sbin/auditd /sbin/augenrules

title: Ensure overlay kernel module is not available
description: The Linux overlay kernel module, commonly referred to as Overlayfs, is a union mount filesystem. It allows the user to overlay one file system on top of another, and creates a single, unified view.
reference: CIS SUSE Linux Enterprise 16 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1.7

audit.command: m=overlay; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/overlay*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Unload and disable the overlay kernel module. 1. Run the following commands to unload the overlay kernel module: # modprobe -r overlay 2>/dev/null # rmmod overlay 2>/dev/null 2. Perform the following to disable the overlay kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install overlay /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "install overlay /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60- overlay.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist overlay in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '%s\n' "" "blacklist overlay" >> /etc/modprobe.d/60-overlay.conf

title: Ensure weak dependencies are configured
description: The RPM packaging specification allows for 3 levels of dependencies to be declared: • hard dependencies (Requires / Provides) for packages which must be installed for a minimal installation of the application to function • weak dependencies (Recommends / Supplements) for packages which provide additional features, but which are not required for a minimal installation to function • hints (Suggests / Enhances) for packages which offer add-ons which might be useful.
reference: CIS SUSE Linux Enterprise 16 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1.5

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Pi -- '"'"'^\h*solver.onlyRequires\h*=\h*true\b'"'"' /etc/zypp/zypp.conf' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'solver.onlyRequires = true' || { echo step1: missing 'solver.onlyRequires = true'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit /etc/zypp/zypp.conf and set solver.onlyRequires = true. Example script: #!/usr/bin/env bash { if grep -Pq '^solver.onlyRequires' /etc/zypp/zypp.conf; then sed -i 's/^solver.onlyRequires\s*=\s*.*/solver.onlyRequires = true/' /etc/zypp/zypp.conf else printf '%s\n' "" "solver.onlyRequires = true" >> /etc/zypp/zypp.conf fi }

title: Ensure the SELinux mode is enforcing
description: SELinux can run in enforcing or permissive mode. Enforcing - Is the recommended mode of operation; in enforcing mode SELinux operates normally, enforcing the loaded security policy on the entire system. Note: You can set individual domains to permissive mode while the system runs in enforcing mode. For example, to make the httpd_t domain permissive: # semanage permissive -a httpd_t
reference: CIS SUSE Linux Enterprise 16 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.1.6

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Pi -- '"'"'^\h*SELINUX=enforcing\b'"'"' /etc/selinux/config' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- SELINUX=enforcing || { echo step1: missing SELINUX=enforcing; return 1; }; command -v getenforce >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step2: getenforce not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c getenforce 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- Enforcing || { echo step2: missing Enforcing; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: 1. Reset the security context on the running system: # restorecon -R / 2. Update the SELinux running state to enforcing: Run the following command to create /etc/selinux/.autorelabel: # touch /etc/selinux/.autorelabel 3. Edit /etc/selinux/config and update the SELINUX parameter to SELINUX=enforcing Example: SELINUX=enforcing 4.Run the following command to reboot the system: # reboot WARNING: The autorelabel may be a long running process and require significant downtime. This should be planed for before executing the reboot! Note: Changing the SELinux mode temporarily can be done via the command setenforce 1

title: Ensure Xwayland is configured
description: Xwayland is a compatibility layer that allows legacy X11 applications to run within a Wayland environment. It's effectively an X server that runs as a Wayland client, enabling existing X11 software to be displayed on a Wayland compositor.
reference: CIS SUSE Linux Enterprise 16 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.8.7

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v sed >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: sed not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'sed -n '"'"'/\[daemon\]/,/\[/p'"'"' /etc/gdm/custom.conf | grep -Psi '"'"'^\h*waylandenable\b'"'"'' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- WaylandEnable=false || { echo step1: missing WaylandEnable=false; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

Be aware that there are programs which consult this file to find out if a user is a normal user; for example, FTP daemons traditionally disallow access to users with shells not included in this file.
reference: CIS SUSE Linux Enterprise 16 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.3.1

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep -Ps '"'"'^\h*([^#\n\r]+)?\/nologin\b'"'"' /etc/shells' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$o" ] || { echo "step1: $o" | head -c 300; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

reference: CIS SUSE Linux Enterprise 16 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2.1.2

title: Ensure the audit configuration is immutable
description: Set system audit so that audit rules cannot be modified with auditctl . Setting the flag "-e 2" forces audit to be put in immutable mode. Audit changes can only be made on system reboot.

title: Ensure overlay kernel module is not available
description: overlay is a Linux filesystem that layers multiple filesystems to create a single unified view which allows a user to "merge" several mount points into a unified filesystem.
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 1.1.1.6

audit.command: m=overlay; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/overlay*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance:
Run the following to unload and disable the overlay kernel module: # modprobe -r overlay 2>/dev/null # rmmod overlay 2>/dev/null Perform the following to disable the overlay kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install overlay /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '
%s
' "install overlay /bin/false" >> overlay.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist overlay in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory Example: # printf '
%s
' "blacklist overlay" >> overlay.conf

title: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is configured

If an audit event is logged which would grow the queue beyond this limit, then a failure occurs and is handled according to the system configuration

title: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is configured

The kernel boot parameter audit_backlog_limit=N, with N representing the amount of messages, will ensure that a queue cannot grow beyond a certain size. If an audit event is logged which would grow the queue beyond this limit, then a failure occurs and is handled according to the system configuration
reference: CIS Ubuntu Linux 22.04 LTS Benchmark v3.0.0 - 6.2.1.4

tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; }
tma_audit_pkg() {
  command -v auditctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f /etc/audit/auditd.conf ] && return 0
  if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then tma_pkg_install auditd; else tma_pkg_install audit; fi; }
tma_nl() { [ -s "$1" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c1 "$1")" ] && echo >> "$1"; return 0; }
tma_kv() { # file key value : 'key = value' style (auditd.conf); replaces every uncommented line
  f=$1; k=$2; v=$3
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
  tma_bak "$f"
  if grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*$k[[:space:]]*=" "$f"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^[[:space:]]*$k[[:space:]]*=.*|$k = $v|" "$f"
  else tma_nl "$f"; printf '%s = %s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"; fi; }
tma_ini_set() { # file section key value : systemd ini 'Key=value'
  f=$1; s=$2; k=$3; v=$4
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; [ -f "$f" ] || : > "$f"; tma_nl "$f"
  sed -i -E "/^[[:space:]]*$k[[:space:]]*=/d" "$f"
  if grep -q "^\[$s\]" "$f"; then sed -i "/^\[$s\]/a $k=$v" "$f"; else printf '[%s]\n%s=%s\n' "$s" "$k" "$v" >> "$f"; fi; }
tma_clear() { # path octal-mask : remove the mask bits from the file mode
  [ -e "$1" ] || return 0
  m=$(stat -Lc %a "$1")
  [ $((8#$m & 8#$2)) -eq 0 ] || chmod "$(printf '%o' $((8#$m & ~8#$2 & 8#7777)))" "$1"; }
tma_rule() { # rules.d-filename audit-rule-line : append when missing (whitespace-normalised)
  f=/etc/audit/rules.d/$1; shift; l=$*
  mkdir -p /etc/audit/rules.d; [ -f "$f" ] || : > "$f"
  if ! tr -s ' \t' '  ' < "$f" | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- "$l"; then tma_nl "$f"; printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$f"; fi
  chown root:root "$f"; chmod 640 "$f"; }
tma_rules_load() { command -v augenrules >/dev/null 2>&1 && augenrules --load >/dev/null 2>&1; true; }
tma_audit_logdir() {
  d=$(awk -F= '/^[[:space:]]*log_file[[:space:]]*=/{print $2}' /etc/audit/auditd.conf 2>/dev/null | xargs 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$d" ] && dirname "$d" || echo /var/log/audit; }
tma_grub_arg() { # key=value : add/replace in GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX and regenerate grub.cfg
  a=$1; k=${a%%=*}; g=/etc/default/grub
  [ -f "$g" ] || { echo "no $g: bootloader not managed by grub defaults" >&2; return 0; }
  tma_bak "$g"
  if ! grep -q '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$g"; then tma_nl "$g"; printf 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="%s"\n' "$a" >> "$g"
  elif grep -E '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$g" | grep -Eq "[\"' ]$k(=|[\"' ])"; then
    sed -i -E "/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#([\"' ])$k(=[^\"' ]*)?([\"' ])#\1$a\3#" "$g"
  else
    sed -i -E "/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#([\"'])\$#  $a\1#; /^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#=([\"'])  #=\1#; /^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#   *# #g" "$g"
  fi
  if command -v update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-grub >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v grub2-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for c in /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/efi/EFI/*/grub.cfg; do [ -f "$c" ] && grub2-mkconfig -o "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  elif command -v grub-mkconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg >/dev/null 2>&1; fi
  true; }
command -v aide >/dev/null 2>&1 || tma_pkg_install aide
sbin=$(readlink -f /sbin)
if [ -f /etc/aide.conf ]; then cf=/etc/aide.conf
elif [ -f /etc/aide/aide.conf ]; then cf=/etc/aide/aide.conf
else echo "AIDE configuration file not found" >&2; exit 0; fi
tma_bak "$cf"
tmp=$cf.tmaegis.new
grep -Ev '^[[:space:]]*(/usr)?/sbin/(auditctl|auditd|ausearch|aureport|autrace|augenrules)[[:space:]]|^# Audit Tools$' "$cf" > "$tmp"
tma_nl "$tmp"
{ echo '# Audit Tools'

  done; } >> "$tmp"
cat "$tmp" > "$cf"; rm -f "$tmp"; true

title: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is configured

  elif grep -E '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' "$g" | grep -Eq "[\"' ]$k(=|[\"' ])"; then
    sed -i -E "/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=/ s#([\"' ])$k(=[^\"' ]*)?([\"' ])#\1$a\3#" "$g"
  else

sbin=$(readlink -f /sbin)

elif [ -f /etc/aide/aide.conf ]; then cf=/etc/aide/aide.conf

tmp=$cf.tmaegis.new
grep -Ev '^[[:space:]]*(/usr)?/sbin/(auditctl|auditd|ausearch|aureport|autrace|augenrules)[[:space:]]|^# Audit Tools$' "$cf" > "$tmp"
tma_nl "$tmp"
{ echo '# Audit Tools'
  for t in auditctl auditd ausearch aureport autrace augenrules; do
    echo "$sbin/$t p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512"
    [ "$sbin" != /sbin ] && echo "/sbin/$t p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512"
  done; } >> "$tmp"
cat "$tmp" > "$cf"; rm -f "$tmp"; true
